problems.problem:
There are some methods to identify extrasolar planets, all with their limitations, of course. One of them is the detection of the variation of the radial velocity of the star, due to the presence of a planet around it. That is, when the plane of the orbit of the extrasolar planet is along the line of sight from the Earth, the star alternately approaches and recedes from us. This oscillation can be observed in its spectrum and from it the mass of the planet that this star has can be determined. This oscillation occurs because both (star and planet) revolve around the centre of mass (CM) or barycentre of the system. In the figure beside we represent the star 51 Pegasi, in the constellation of Pegasus, of apparent magnitude 5.5, at a distance of 51 light-years, of mass $M = 2.2\times10^{30}$ kg and its orbit, almost circular (dashed line), and its planet called 51 Pegasi b, with orbital period 4.2 days, of mass $m = 9.5\times10^{26}$ kg and its orbit (also almost circular). Note that: $M = 2316\,m$. The centres of mass of the star and of the planet are separated, on average, by the distance $d = 8\times10^{6}$ km.

4a) (0.5 point) What is the distance from the centre of 51 Pegasi to the barycentre of the system? Let us help. You know that when you are on a seesaw and on the other side there is someone heavier than you, that person needs to stay closer to the centre of the seesaw and you farther from its centre, if you wish, for example, to keep the seesaw still with both balanced horizontally. There is an equation relating their masses ($m_a$ and $m_b$) and respective distances ($r_a$ and $r_b$) to the centre of the seesaw for it to be in equilibrium: $m_a r_a = m_b r_b$. Do you understand now? Just put the star and the planet on the seesaw. Answer 4a): ........ km

4b) (0.25 point) The orbital period of 51 Pegasi b is 4.2 days. What is the orbital period of 51 Pegasi? Note: no calculation is needed. Answer 4b): ........ days

4c) (0.25 point) Make an X on the dashed circle where 51 Pegasi will be when 51 Pegasi b is at the position X indicated in the figure above. Note: of course no calculation is needed either.

problems.problem_orig:
Existem alguns métodos para identificar planetas extrassolares, todos com suas limitações, claro. Um deles é o da detecção da variação da velocidade radial da estrela, devido à presença de um planeta ao seu redor. Ou seja, quando o plano da órbita do planeta extrassolar está na direção da linha de visada da Terra, a estrela ora se aproxima e ora se afasta de nós. Esta oscilação pode ser observada no seu espectro e com isso pode-se determinar a massa do planeta que esta estrela possui. Esta oscilação ocorre porque ambos (estrela e planeta) giram em torno do centro de massa (CM) ou baricentro do sistema. Na figura ao lado representamos a estrela 51 Pegasi, da constelação de Pégaso, de magnitude aparente 5,5, distante 51 anos-luz, de massa $M = 2{,}2\times10^{30}$ kg e sua órbita, quase circular (linha tracejada) e seu planeta chamado 51 Pegasi b, com período orbital de 4,2 dias, de massa $m = 9{,}5\times10^{26}$ kg e sua órbita (também quase circular). Note que: $M = 2.316\,m$. Os centros de massa da estrela e do planeta estão separados, em média, pela distância $d = 8\times10^{6}$ km.

4a) (0,5 ponto) Qual é a distância do centro da 51 Pegasi ao baricentro do sistema? Vamos ajudar. Você sabe que quando está numa gangorra e do outro lado está alguém mais pesado que você, ele precisa ficar mais perto do centro da gangorra e você mais longe do centro dela, se desejarem, por exemplo, deixar a gangorra parada com ambos equilibrados na horizontal. Existe uma equação que relaciona suas massas ($m_a$ e $m_b$) e respectivas distâncias ($r_a$ e $r_b$) ao centro da gangorra para que ela fique em equilíbrio: $m_a r_a = m_b r_b$. Já entendeu, certo? É só colocar estrela e planeta na gangorra. Resposta 4a): ........ km

4b) (0,25 ponto) O período orbital de 51 Pegasi b é de 4,2 dias. Qual é o período orbital de 51 Pegasi? Obs. Não precisa fazer nenhuma conta. Resposta 4b): ........ dias

4c) (0,25 ponto) Faça um X no círculo tracejado onde estará 51 Pegasi quando 51 Pegasi b estiver na posição X indicada na figura acima. Obs. Claro que também não precisa fazer nenhuma conta.

problems.problem:
Another method used to detect extrasolar planets is known as the planetary transit method. Since stars are much larger than planets and emit light, the brightness of the star is slightly reduced by the blocking that the disc of the planet causes during its transit, as the figure beside illustrates (brightness versus time). About 75% of the extrasolar planets discovered so far (about 3600) were found by this method. In February 2017 the discovery, by the transit method, of the extrasolar planetary system TRAPPIST-1 was announced, with seven terrestrial-type planets around it, 4 of them of size similar to the Earth and three of them within the so-called habitable zone. All planets, including the extrasolar ones, must obey Kepler's third law, which is given by:

$$\frac{T^2}{D^3}=\frac{4\pi^2}{G(M+m)}=K$$

where $T$ is the period of the planet, $D$ its mean distance to the star, $M$ the mass of the star, $m$ the mass of the planet, $\pi\cong 3.14$, $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}\ \text{kg}^{-1}\,\text{m}^3\,\text{s}^{-2}$ and $K$ is the Kepler constant.

5a) (0.5 point) Calling $K_S$ the constant for the Solar System and $K_T$ that for the Trappist-1 System, calculate the ratio between $K_S$ and $K_T$, that is, calculate $\dfrac{K_S}{K_T}$.
Data: The orbital period of the Earth ($T$) is 360 days (to simplify the calculations) and its mean distance to the Sun ($D$) is 1 AU (Astronomical Unit). The orbital period of planet "d" ($T_d$) of Trappist-1 is 4 days and its mean distance to Trappist-1 ($D_d$) is 0.02 AU. Since stars have much more mass than planets, neglect $m$ in Kepler's law. Use $M_S$ for the mass of the Sun and $M_T$ for the mass of Trappist-1.

5b) (0.5 point) Calculate how many times the mass of the star Trappist-1, $M_T$, is smaller than that of the Sun, $M_S$, that is, find $\dfrac{M_T}{M_S}$.

Outro método usado para detectar planetas extrassolares é conhecido pelo nome de método de trânsito planetário. Como as estrelas são muito maiores do que os planetas e emitem luz, o brilho da estrela fica ligeiramente reduzido pelo bloqueio que o disco do planeta causa durante o seu trânsito, como ilustra a figura ao lado (brilho em função do tempo). Cerca de 75% dos planetas extrassolares descobertos até o momento (cerca de 3.600) o foram por este método. Em fevereiro de 2017 foi anunciada a descoberta, pelo método do trânsito, do sistema planetário extrassolar TRAPPIST-1 com sete planetas, tipo terrestre, ao seu redor, sendo 4 de tamanho similar à Terra e três deles dentro da chamada zona de habitabilidade. Todos os planetas, incluindo os extrassolares, devem obedecer à terceira lei de Kepler, a qual é dada por:

$$\frac{T^2}{D^3}=\frac{4\pi^2}{G(M+m)}=K$$

onde $T$ é o período do planeta, $D$ sua distância média à estrela, $M$ a massa da estrela, $m$ a massa do planeta, $\pi\cong 3{,}14$, $G = 6{,}67\times10^{-11}\ \text{kg}^{-1}\,\text{m}^3\,\text{s}^{-2}$ e $K$ é a constante de Kepler.

O período orbital do planeta "d" ($T_d$) de Trappist-1 é de 4 dias e sua distância média a Trappist-1 ($D_d$) é de 0,02 UA. problems.problem:
The VSB-30 is a Brazilian rocket, developed by the Institute of Aeronautics and Space (IAE), capable of taking payloads to space. It is the burning of the propellant (mixture of fuel and oxidiser) that provides the thrust needed to take the payload to the apogee of 250 km. The total mass of the VSB-30 is 2850 kg, of which 1650 kg is propellant. The 1st stage works for 12 seconds. The ignition of the 2nd stage motor occurs 15 seconds into the flight. It is during these 3 seconds that the 1st stage motor separates from the 2nd stage motor, falling into the sea.

During the propelled flight of the VSB-30, three forces act on the rocket: Weight ($P$), Thrust ($E$) and Drag ($A$). The force $P$ results from the action of gravity. The force $E$ results from Newton's 3rd Law, that is, the expulsion of the gases expelled by the running motor makes the rocket move in the opposite sense. Finally there is the drag, which results from the interaction of the rocket with the Earth's atmosphere.

8a) (0.5 point) At 6 seconds of flight the VSB-30 is at 1 km altitude, flying vertically at a speed of 1000 km/h. Considering that at this instant the total mass of the VSB-30 is 2500 kg, $E = 103000$ N and $A = 3000$ N, use Newton's 2nd Law ($F = m \times a$) to calculate the acceleration of the VSB-30 at this instant. Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$. Note: record your calculations below; without them the result is not accepted. Answer 8a): ........

8b) (0.25 point) The upper part of the 1st stage of the VSB-30 is fitted into the lower part of the 2nd stage. Something similar to the fitting of a ballpoint pen inside its cap. What keeps the 1st and 2nd stages together is the balance of the forces acting on each stage, including the contact force represented by the vector $N$ in the figures beside. $A_1$ and $A_2$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ represent the drag forces and the weight forces acting on the 1st and 2nd stages, respectively. $E$ is the thrust force generated by the 1st stage. O VSB-30 é um foguete brasileiro, desenvolvido pelo Instituto de Aeronáutica e Espaço (IAE), capaz de levar cargas úteis ao espaço. É a queima do propelente (mistura de combustível e oxidante) que fornece o empuxo necessário para levar a carga útil ao apogeu de 250 km. A massa total do VSB-30 é de 2.850 kg, sendo 1.650 kg de propelente. O 1º estágio funciona por 12 segundos. O acionamento do motor do 2º estágio ocorre aos 15 segundos de voo. É durante esses 3 segundos que o motor do 1º estágio separa-se do motor do 2º estágio, caindo no mar.

Durante o voo de propulsão do VSB-30, três forças atuam sobre o foguete: Peso ($P$), Empuxo ($E$), e Arrasto ($A$). A força $P$ resulta da ação da gravidade. A força $E$ resulta da 3ª Lei de Newton, ou seja, a expulsão dos gases expelidos pelo motor em funcionamento faz com que o foguete se mova em sentido oposto. Finalmente tem-se o arrasto, que resulta da interação do foguete com a atmosfera terrestre.

8a) (0,5 ponto) Aos 6 segundos de voo o VSB-30 encontra-se a 1 km de altitude, voando verticalmente à velocidade de 1.000 km/h. Considerando-se que nesse instante a massa total do VSB-30 é 2.500 kg, $E = 103.000$ N e $A = 3.000$ N, utilize a 2ª Lei de Newton ($F = m \times a$) para calcular a aceleração do VSB-30 neste instante. In 2017 the Geostationary Defence and Strategic Communications Satellite (SGDC) was launched. The SGDC was contracted by the Government of Brazil from Visiona Tecnologia Espacial, a national company located in São José dos Campos, SP. The SGDC is located in the equatorial plane of the Earth, 35800 km from its surface. At this great distance it revolves around the Earth with the same angular speed with which the Earth rotates about its axis. Therefore, everything happens as if the SGDC were at rest relative to a fixed point on the Earth's surface. The SGDC is "parked" at 75$^\circ$ West longitude.

Although TV transmission is the main application of geostationary satellites, new technologies allow their use for the transmission of Internet signals, which require, among other things, more power compared with TV. To receive and send signals (electromagnetic waves) the SGDC is equipped with several antennas, some operating in the X band (from 7 to 8 GHz, Giga Hertz = $10^9$ Hz) and several in the Ka band (from 17 to 30 GHz). While the X band is used for military communications (telephony, data, voice and image) the Ka band is used for the Internet.

Instead of using a single "beam" (Figure A), the SGDC projects 67 beams in the Ka band, of about 500 km diameter each. To simplify, only some of these beams are shown in Figure B. In this way, the power of the signal received by each of these regions is much higher than that which would be received if the satellite transmitted using a single beam. It is exactly this multiple-beam technology that allows the use of the SGDC for Internet transmission. On the ground there will be large antennas pointed at the satellites. They are called Gateways, represented by small black circles in Figure B, in beams 15, 24, 33, 36 and 44.

Question 9) (0.2 for each correct answer) Based on this information write C (Correct) or E (Wrong) for each of the statements below:

( ) The same satellite can carry out transmission of data, voice, images and Internet.
( ) The island of Fernando de Noronha is not in the coverage area of the SGDC.
( ) A Brazilian vessel in the Atlantic, outside the Ka-band coverage region of the SGDC satellite, can enjoy the broadband data connection provided by this satellite.
( ) Supposing that the data transmission rate of the SGDC to a certain user is 5 Mbps (Megabit per second), the download of a 50 MB file (MB $\rightarrow$ MegaByte = $10^6$ Byte, with 1 Byte = 8 bits) will take 10 seconds.
( ) Beams 41, 42, 36, 32, 37, 27, 23 and 18 have part or all of their coverage area over the sea. Thus, vessels and oil platforms located in these areas can use the SGDC for Internet connection.

problems.problem:
The light bulbs in homes have printed on them their respective Powers, for example 60 Watt, 100 Watt etc., which defines their "luminosity". Watt, W, is the unit of Power and represents the amount of energy emitted per unit time, that is: Power (W) = Energy (J)/time (s). Stars are big light bulbs, but we call their Power Luminosity ($L$), that is: Luminosity (W) = Energy (J)/time (s). The Power of a light bulb is always the same, no matter whether we are near or far from it. Luminosity is also a property of the star. It also does not depend on whether we are near or far from it. The Power of a light bulb depends on the resistance, current and potential difference. The Luminosity ($L$) of a star depends on the Temperature ($T$) of its surface (measured in Kelvin) and on the area of this surface, that is, on the Radius ($R$) of the star, in the following way:

$$L = k\,(4\pi R^2)\,T^4$$

where $k$ is called the Stefan-Boltzmann constant and equals $k = 5.67\times10^{-8}\ \text{W}\,\text{m}^{-2}\,\text{K}^{-4}$.

Question 3) Calculate the exact value of the Luminosity of the Sun in Watt. Data: Radius of the Sun: about 700000 km. Surface temperature of the Sun: about 6000 K. Ask for more paper if you need more space for the calculations, but attach everything to the paper. Answer 3): ........ W

problems.problem:
The Luminosity of a star is its Power ($P$), that is, the energy (J) that it emits per second (s). Luminosity is measured in Watt (W), just like Power. A 100 Watt light bulb shines a lot if it is near, but little if it is far, because its energy (light) spreads out through all of space and so, the farther away, the less light (energy) we receive from it. The same happens with stars: the farther away we are, the less energy we receive on one square metre, for example. The figure on the right shows that the Luminosity of the Sun, $L_\odot$, is the same that passes through the imaginary spherical surfaces of radii $d$ or $2d$, but, obviously, the "density" of this Luminosity becomes diluted as we move away from the Sun. This "density" is called Flux ($F$), its unit is Watt/metre$^2$ (W/m$^2$) and it is calculated by the expression:

$$F=\frac{L}{4\pi d^2}$$

where $L$ is the luminosity of the star and $d$ the distance from it to us.

problems.problem:
Blue Moon. As the Moon travels around the Earth, over the month, it goes through a cycle of phases. The complete cycle lasts approximately 29.5 days and is called a Lunation. But we have months with 28, 29, 30 and 31 days, so it can happen that in the same month we have two Full Moons. Obviously this is a rare phenomenon. It is even rarer to have two occurrences of this in the same year, as happened in 2018. A rare event, in the folklore of some countries it is called a Blue Moon. Obviously the Moon does not turn blue, except when there are great volcanic eruptions on the Earth, whose particles suspended in the atmosphere scatter the red and then the Moon becomes slightly bluish in any phase.

Blood Moon. On 31/01/18 there was a total eclipse of the Moon and the press made much use of the term "Blood Moon". An extremely inappropriate term, obviously. In every total lunar eclipse the Moon passes through the cone of shadow cast by the Earth, but despite being in the "shadow" it does not become dark or invisible. The incident solar light on the Earth's atmosphere is almost totally scattered, mainly the blue, which is why we see the sky blue. Red light, having a longer wavelength, is less scattered by our atmosphere and, in fact, passes through it and is refracted into the shadow cone. When it reaches the Moon, it is reflected and we see the Moon reddish. Hence associating the reddish colour with blood on the lunar surface is in extremely bad taste.

Super-Moon. The Moon describes around the Earth an elliptical orbit, of low eccentricity, as the figure beside illustrates in an extremely exaggerated way (the figure shows the Earth at the centre of a flattened ellipse labelled "exaggeratedly flattened lunar orbit", with "Moon at perigee" on the left and "Moon at apogee" on the right). When the Full Moon occurs and it is at perigee (or close to it) its diameter can be up to 14% larger than at apogee and up to 30% brighter. When this happens it is called a super-Moon, however, there is nothing special besides the increase in angular diameter (almost imperceptible) and the greater brightness.

Lua azul. À medida que a Lua viaja ao redor da Terra, ao longo do mês, ela passa por um ciclo de fases. O ciclo completo dura aproximadamente 29,5 dias e é chamado de Lunação. Mas temos meses com 28, 29, 30 e 31 dias, logo, pode ocorrer que num mesmo mês tenhamos duas Luas cheias. Obviamente isso é um fenômeno raro. É ainda mais raro termos duas ocorrências destas num mesmo ano, como aconteceu em 2018. Evento raro, no folclore de alguns países é chamado de Lua azul. Obviamente a Lua não fica azul, exceto quando há grandes erupções vulcânicas na Terra, cujas partículas em suspensão na atmosfera espalham o vermelho e, então, a Lua fica ligeiramente azulada em qualquer fase.

Lua de sangue. Em 31/01/18 houve um eclipse total da Lua e a imprensa se utilizou muito do termo "Lua de sangue". Um termo extremamente inadequado, obviamente. Em todo eclipse lunar total a Lua passa pelo cone de sombra projetado pela Terra, mas apesar de estar na "sombra" ela não fica escura ou invisível. A luz solar incidente sobre a atmosfera terrestre é quase totalmente espalhada, principalmente o azul, tanto é que vemos o céu azul. A luz vermelha, por ter comprimento de onda maior, é menos espalhada pela nossa atmosfera e, de fato, a atravessa e sofre refração indo sobre o cone de sombra. Quando atinge a Lua, é refletida e vemos a Lua avermelhada. Daí associar a cor avermelhada a sangue na superfície lunar é de extremo mau gosto.

Super-Lua. A Lua descreve ao redor da Terra uma órbita elíptica, de baixa excentricidade, conforme ilustra de forma extremamente exagerada a figura ao lado (a figura mostra a Terra no centro de uma elipse achatada rotulada "Órbita lunar exageradamente achatada", com "Lua no perigeu" à esquerda e "Lua no apogeu" à direita). Quando ocorre a Lua cheia e ela está no perigeu (ou próximo dele) ela pode ficar com diâmetro de até 14% maior do que no apogeu e até 30% mais brilhante. Quando isso ocorre ela é chamada de super-Lua, porém, não há nada de especial além do aumento do diâmetro angular (quase imperceptível) e do maior brilho.

In 2017 the 40th anniversary of the launch of the unmanned spacecraft Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 was celebrated. Voyager 1 visited Jupiter and Saturn and is 21 billion km from the Earth. Voyager 2 visited the planets Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, and is currently 17.5 billion km from the Earth. Both remain in operation.

As illustrated in the Figure below on the left, the last stage of the rocket placed Voyager 2 in space at a speed of 36 km/s, this speed measured relative to the Sun. From the moment it is in space, the speed of Voyager 2 decreases significantly through the action of gravity. When passing Jupiter, the speed of Voyager 2 is increased by more than 10 km/s, as shown in the Figure. After this sudden increase, the speed falls again through the action of gravity, until the spacecraft approaches (100000 km distance) Saturn, as shown in the Figure on the right. In this Figure, there is a simplified two-dimensional representation of the trajectory of Voyager 2 past Saturn, relative to the frame fixed on Saturn. Since the passage takes place in a short time relative to the orbital period of Saturn around the Sun, consider Saturn as an inertial reference frame. Consider that $\vec{V}_A$ and $\vec{V}_B$ are the velocity vectors of the Voyager 2 probe at points A and B relative to the reference frame of Saturn and both have magnitude equal to 14 km/s. In the Figure, $\vec{V}_{Sat}$ is the velocity vector of Saturn relative to the frame of the Sun and its magnitude is approximately 10 km/s.

Hint: To solve some of the questions below, remember that velocity is a vector quantity, that is, it is characterised by its magnitude, direction and sense. Therefore, when adding or subtracting velocities, make a representation of the vectors, adding or subtracting them according to the question.

Note: Record your calculations in all items. Without them the answer will have no value. Without units you lose 0.05 points in each item.

8a) (0.25 point) Calculate the variation of the magnitude of the velocity of Voyager 2 between points A and B, as represented in the reference frame of Saturn.

8b) (0.25 point) Consider that on passing Point B Voyager 2 has its velocity vector in the same direction and sense as the velocity vector of Saturn relative to the Sun. Considering that the magnitude of the velocity vector of Voyager 2 relative to Saturn is 14 km/s and that the magnitude of the velocity vector of Saturn relative to the Sun is 10 km/s, calculate the magnitude of the velocity of Voyager 2 relative to the Sun.

8c) (0.25 point) Determine the magnitude of the velocity vector of Voyager 2 relative to the Sun, when it is at point A of the Figure. Consider that the vectors $\vec{V}_A$ and $\vec{V}_{Sat}$ are perpendicular and use: $\sqrt{296} = 17.2$.

8d) (0.25 point) Calculate the variation in the magnitude of the velocity of Voyager 2 between points A and B, measured relative to the Sun. Is it possible to conclude that Saturn added or removed kinetic energy to Voyager 2, with respect to the frame of the Sun? Note: without the conclusion you lose 0.1 point.

problems.problem:
In 2017 the Geostationary Defence and Strategic Communications Satellite (SGDC) was launched. The SGDC is operated by the Brazilian government and aims to offer broadband Internet access to remote regions of Brazil, as well as to provide a means of secure communication to the Brazilian Armed Forces. The SGDC system was developed under the responsibility of the company Visiona Tecnologia Espacial, of São José dos Campos, SP.

Because of its orbit, the SGDC stays "still" relative to the Earth at a distance of 35800 km. The user, connected to Station A, can establish communication, via SGDC, with another user, connected to Station B (see Figure). In the uplink and downlink communication links two important phenomena occur. One of them is the reduction of the signal intensity, $E$, as a function of distance and of the interactions of the electromagnetic waves with the medium in which they propagate. Another phenomenon is the electromagnetic noise, $N$, which are spurious signals that introduce undesired contributions to the communications.

Based on these concepts the signal-to-noise ratio ($E/N$) is established:

$$\frac{E}{N}=\frac{P\times G}{R\times L}$$

where $P$ = transmission power of the satellite, $G$ = Gain of the receiving antenna of station B, $L$ = Transmission losses and $R$ = Bit rate, that is, bits per second (bps). The higher this ratio, the better the capture of the information at the receiver. In this exercise, the communication link to be analysed is between the Satellite (transmitter) and Station B (receiver), in the downlink sense. Station B comprises an antenna of 5 m diameter. (The Figure shows the satellite, Stations A and B, the uplink and downlink paths, the loss $L$ and the gain $G_r$.)

9a) (0.5 point) Suppose a situation in which the SGDC is transmitting data at the rate of one million bits per second ($R = 1$ Mbps) with $P = 50$ W. Because of a torrential rain, the total loss ($L$) has its value doubled. Supposing that even with the rain one wants to keep the same data transmission rate between the SGDC and Station B, what would be the new transmission power of the satellite? Consider that the signal-to-noise ratio does not change and that the antenna of Station B is the same.

9b) (0.5 point) On being presented with the new power value, an SGDC engineer reported that the satellite was already operating at its power limit, which is 50 W. Alternatively, he proposed that the increase of the losses ($L$) be solved by increasing the gain ($G$) of the antenna of Station B. Among the factors that impact the gain of the antenna is its size. The gain is given by $G = c \times A$, where $c$ is a constant and $A$ is the circular area of the antenna. Considering that the satellite operates at its maximum power, what is the new diameter of the antenna to maintain the signal-to-noise ratio and, thus, the same data transmission rate? The original diameter ($D_1$) of the antenna is 5 m.
Use: $\sqrt{2} = 1.4$.

Em 2017 foi lançado o Satélite Geoestacionário de Defesa e Comunicações Estratégicas (SGDC). O SGDC é operado pelo governo brasileiro e visa oferecer acesso à Internet banda-larga a regiões remotas do Brasil, bem como disponibilizar um meio de comunicação segura às Forças Armadas brasileiras. O sistema SGDC foi desenvolvido sob responsabilidade da empresa Visiona Tecnologia Espacial, de São José dos Campos, SP.

Em função da sua órbita, o SGDC fica "parado" em relação à Terra a 35.800 km de distância. O usuário, ligado à Estação A, pode estabelecer comunicação, via SGDC, com outro usuário, conectado à Estação B (vide Figura). Nos enlaces de comunicação de uplink e downlink ocorrem dois fenômenos importantes. Um deles é a redução da intensidade do sinal, $E$, em função da distância e das interações das ondas eletromagnéticas com o meio no qual elas se propagam. Outro fenômeno é o ruído eletromagnético, $N$, que são sinais espúrios que introduzem contribuições indesejadas nas comunicações.

Baseado nesses conceitos é estabelecida a relação sinal/ruído ($E/N$):

$$\frac{E}{N}=\frac{P\times G}{R\times L}$$

onde $P$ = Potência de transmissão do satélite, $G$ = Ganho da antena receptora da estação B, $L$ = Perdas na transmissão e $R$ = Taxa de bits, isto é, bits por segundo (bps). Quanto maior essa relação, melhor a captação da informação no receptor. Nesse exercício, o enlace de comunicação a ser analisado é entre o Satélite (transmissor) e a Estação B (receptor), no sentido de downlink. A Estação B compreende uma antena com 5 m de diâmetro. (A Figura mostra o satélite, as Estações A e B, os caminhos de uplink e downlink, a perda $L$ e o ganho $G_r$.)

9a) (0,5 ponto) Suponha uma situação na qual o SGDC esteja transmitindo dados à taxa de um milhão de bits por segundo ($R = 1$ Mbps) com $P = 50$ W. Em função de uma chuva torrencial, a perda total ($L$) tem seu valor dobrado. Supondo que mesmo com a chuva se queira manter a mesma taxa de transmissão de dados entre o SGDC e a Estação B, qual seria a nova potência de transmissão do satélite? Considere que a relação sinal/ruído não se altere e que a antena da Estação B é a mesma.

9b) (0,5 ponto) Ao ser apresentado com o novo valor de potência, um engenheiro do SGDC informou que o satélite já operava no seu limite de potência, que é de 50 W. Alternativamente, ele propôs que o aumento das perdas ($L$) fosse resolvido aumentando-se o ganho ($G$) da antena da Estação B. Dentre os fatores que impactam no ganho da antena está o seu tamanho. O ganho é dado por $G = c \times A$, onde $c$ é uma constante e $A$ é a área circular da antena. Considerando-se que o satélite opere na sua potência máxima, qual o novo diâmetro da antena para manter a relação sinal/ruído e, assim, a mesma taxa de transmissão de dados? O diâmetro ($D_1$) original da antena é de 5 m.
Use: $\sqrt{2} = 1{,}4$.

With the development of astronautics it is increasingly easy to put telescopes in orbit. However, some, such as SOHO (Solar and Heliospheric Observatory), need to revolve around the Sun with the same period as the Earth and stay between the Sun and the Earth, because they need to observe the Sun 24 h/day. But by Kepler's third law $T^2 = k\,D^3$, that is, the smaller the distance to the Sun, the smaller the period will be and vice versa. So, it would not be possible to put SOHO and other satellites to revolve around the Sun, with the same period as the Earth, in a place different from the Earth. But the Italian Joseph-Louis de Lagrange, in 1772, discovered that there are five points, called Lagrangian points, in an Earth-Sun system, or Earth-Moon, or Sun-planet, that are "special". The point $L_1$ lies on the Earth-Sun line, between Earth and Sun, and an observatory placed there moves with the same period as the Earth, as SOHO does, which is never eclipsed by the Moon and always receives the same irradiation from the Sun. See the figure beside. The point $L_2$ lies beyond the cone of shadow (umbra) of the Earth, will be the location of the James Webb Space Telescope and will have a period of translation equal to that of the Earth. The points $L_4$ and $L_5$ lie on the orbit of the Earth and are located by an equilateral triangle with edge equal to the Earth-Sun distance. (The figure shows the orbit of $M_2$ around $M_1$, supposing $M_1 \gg M_2$, with $M_1$ at the centre, $M_2$ on the circle, the points $L_1$, $L_2$, $L_3$ on the line through $M_1$ and $M_2$, $L_4$ and $L_5$ on the circle at $60^\circ$ from that line.)

10a) (0.5 point) Consider that $M_1$ is the mass of the Sun, $M_2$ the mass of the Earth, $R$ the Earth-Sun distance and $r$ the distance from the Earth to the Lagrangian points $L_1$ and $L_2$ (they are symmetric with respect to $M_2$). It can be shown that $r$ is given by:

$$r \approx \sqrt[3]{\frac{M_2}{3M_1}}\,R, \qquad R = 1.4784\times10^{8}\ \text{km}.$$

Knowing that the mean distance to the Moon is 384000 km, calculate how many times $r$ is farther than the orbit of the Moon.

10b) (0.5 point) As explained, the advantage of the points $L_1$, $L_2$ and $L_3$ is that even though they are at different distances from the Earth to the Sun, satellites placed there would have the same period of translation as the Earth around the Sun, that is, 365.25 days. What would be the period of translation of satellites placed at the Lagrangian points $L_4$ and $L_5$? The answer is only valid with a justification.

The luminosity of a star is a characteristic of its own and depends only on its radius and its surface temperature. Its brightness, on the other hand, depends on its distance from us. We can compare the luminosity of a star to the power of an ordinary light bulb. A lit 60-watt bulb, for example, will always have 60 watts at whatever distance it is from us. However, it will be brighter the closer it is to us.

The luminosity $L$ of a star is proportional to its radius, $R$, squared and to its surface temperature, $T$, raised to the fourth power.

If we adopt solar units, that is, if we measure $L$ in units of solar luminosity ($L_{Sun}$), $R$ in units of solar radius ($R_{Sun}$) and $T$ in units of solar temperature (6000 K), we can write an equation to calculate the radius of a star in comparison with the radius of the Sun:

$$L\ (\text{in solar luminosities}) = R^2\ (\text{in solar radii}) \times T^4\ (\text{in units of 6000 K}) \ \rightarrow\ R = \frac{\sqrt{L}}{T^2}$$

Let us give an example: Spica, in the constellation of Virgo, is 12100 times more luminous than the Sun ($L = 12100\,L_{Sun}$) and has a surface temperature of 22200 K ($T = 22200/6000 = 3.7\,T_{Sun}$). Therefore, its radius will be:

$$R = \frac{\sqrt{12100}}{3.7^2} = \frac{110}{13.69} \cong 8\,R_{Sun}\quad (\text{8 times the radius of the Sun})$$

A luminosidade de uma estrela é uma característica própria dela e depende apenas do seu raio e da sua temperatura superficial. Já o seu brilho depende da distância dela até nós. Podemos comparar a luminosidade de uma estrela à potência de uma lâmpada comum. Uma lâmpada de 60 watts acesa, por exemplo, terá sempre 60 watts a qualquer distância que esteja de nós. No entanto ela será mais brilhante quanto mais perto estiver de nós.

A luminosidade $L$ de uma estrela é proporcional ao seu raio, $R$, elevado ao quadrado e à sua temperatura, $T$, superficial elevada à quarta potência.

Se adotarmos as unidades solares, ou seja, se medirmos $L$ em unidades de luminosidade solar ($L_{Sol}$), $R$ em unidades de raio solar ($R_{Sol}$) e $T$ em unidades de temperatura solar (6000 K) podemos escrever uma equação para calcular o raio de uma estrela em comparação com o raio do Sol:

$$L\ (\text{em luminosidades solares}) = R^2\ (\text{em raios solares}) \times T^4\ (\text{em unidades de 6000 K}) \ \rightarrow\ R = \frac{\sqrt{L}}{T^2}$$

Vamos dar um exemplo: Spica, da Constelação da Virgem, é 12.100 vezes mais luminosa do que o Sol ($L = 12.100\,L_{Sol}$) e possui temperatura superficial de 22.200 K ($T = 22.200/6000 = 3{,}7\,T_{Sol}$). Logo, seu raio será:

$$R = \frac{\sqrt{12.100}}{3{,}7^2} = \frac{110}{13{,}69} \cong 8\,R_{Sol}\quad (\text{8 vezes o raio do Sol})$$

Kepler studied the observations collected over more than 20 years by the astronomer Tycho Brahe (1546 - 1601) and discovered, around 1605, that the planets followed three mathematical laws:

- The third Law (harmonic) relates the square of the orbital period of the planets directly to the cube of their mean distance to the Sun.

The Theory of Relativity states that the mass of bodies deforms the space near them, so that a light ray is deflected by the deformation. This "bending of light" could only be observed through a total eclipse of the Sun, that is, when the Moon lies between the Sun and the Earth, projecting its shadow on part of the planet. With the eclipse, the dazzling light of the Sun disappears and one can see the brightness of the nearby stars.

We know that astronomers can use radar measurements, parallax and even Kepler's Laws to determine the distance of the objects of the Solar System. Knowing the distance, we can convert the angular size of a body into its physical size using only geometry. In the drawing, a large circle was centred on the observer passing through the object (the figure shows the observer, the distant object, its unknown diameter, the measured angular diameter, the known distance, the $360^\circ$ turn and the circumference $= 2\pi\times$ distance).

This question is related to the previous question, which is why you should use the figure of question 9 to help your understanding of this text. Stage 2 is known as the parking orbit, located at 200 km distance from the surface of the Earth. During the more than two hours they remain in this orbit, the astronauts and also the teams on Earth check all the systems of the rocket. If everything is OK, the motor of the 3rd stage of the Saturn V is fired for the second time, for about 6 minutes, injecting the spacecraft into the translunar trajectory, that is, towards a point in space where the Moon will be 80 hours later. A few minutes later, the motor of the 3rd stage is discarded, becoming space junk.

10a) (0.5 point) The force of gravity is given by $F = \dfrac{m M_T G}{r^2}$, where $r$ is the distance from the spacecraft to the centre of the Earth, $m$ is the mass of what remained of the Saturn V, $M_T$ is the mass of the Earth and $G$ is the gravitational constant. While in circular parking orbit, what remained of the Saturn V will be subject to a radial (or centripetal) acceleration given by $a = \dfrac{(V_{orbital})^2}{r}$. Using Newton's 2nd Law, calculate the orbital speed, in km/s, of what remained of the Saturn V in the parking orbit. Disregard any forces other than the gravitational one.
To simplify, consider $M_T G = 416000\ \text{km}^3/\text{s}^2$, the radius of the Earth $R_T = 6300$ km and that the force and acceleration have the same direction. Pay attention to the units!

The escape velocity is the speed that a body needs to reach to leave the Earth's gravitational field and reach infinity with zero speed. This is equivalent to the initial speed that makes the sum of gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy zero.

problems.problem:
Kepler's three Laws (1571 – 1630) describe the motions of planets, moons, comets, artificial satellites etc. and, for the planets, say the following:
1st Law (Law of orbits): The orbit of each planet is an ellipse, with the Sun at one of the foci.
2nd Law (Law of areas): A straight line between the Sun and the planet "sweeps" equal areas in equal time intervals.
3rd Law (Law of periods): The square of the orbital Period ($P$) divided by the cube of the mean distance ($D$) of the planet to the Sun is a constant ($k$), that is,
$$P^2/D^3 = k.$$
The figure beside shows the scheme of the orbits of the first 6 planets of the Solar System, at the correct distance scale, where $1.0\ \text{cm} \equiv 1.0\ \text{AU}$ (the figure is a ruler laid over the orbits, with the distances 1.0 cm, 1.5 cm, 5.2 cm and 9.5 cm marked).

Note that the constant $k$ is the same for all bodies that orbit the Sun and depends on the units used to express $P$ and $D$. For example, in the case of the Earth, if we use the period, $P$, in units of EARTH YEARS ($\mathrm{A_T}$), and the mean distance ($D$) to the Sun in ASTRONOMICAL UNITS, AU, which is the distance between the Sun (black dot at the centre of the figure, out of scale) and the Earth (third orbit), then we have:
$$k = \frac{(1\ \mathrm{A_T})^2}{(1\ \mathrm{AU})^3} = 1\ \frac{\mathrm{A_T}^2}{\mathrm{AU}^3}$$

That said, mark with an X the option that gives the approximate period ($P$) of Jupiter (in $\mathrm{A_T}$), given that the mean distance of Jupiter to the Sun, in AU, is in the figure.

( ) 3 $\mathrm{A_T}$
( ) 5.2 $\mathrm{A_T}$
( ) 27 $\mathrm{A_T}$
( ) 12 $\mathrm{A_T}$

problems.problem:
On 24 April 2020 the Hubble Space Telescope completed 30 years in orbit around the Earth. Its planning began in the 1970s, but it was only launched in 1990. On receiving the first images the scientists were perplexed by their poor quality. After some analysis, they discovered that Hubble had a flaw in its primary mirror. NASA engineers decided that astronauts could capture Hubble with the robotic arm of the space shuttle and, by means of extravehicular activities, repair its optical system. After the repairs Hubble was put back into its original orbit. This Hubble repair mission was one of NASA's greatest achievements and, since then, 4 other servicing missions have been carried out. (The figure labels the Hubble Telescope, the robotic arm and the Space Shuttle.)

Question 15) Suppose that, to put Hubble back into its correct orbit, the robotic arm of the space shuttle exerted a force ($F$) of 1 N, whose magnitude, direction and sense were constant throughout the manoeuvre and perpendicular to the direction of motion of the space shuttle. The mass of Hubble ($m_H$) is approximately 10000 kg. Newton's second law says that $F = ma$ ($m$ = mass and $a$ = acceleration).

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration ($a_H$), in m/s$^2$, to which Hubble was subjected in this operation and also calculate the time ($t$), in seconds, taken for Hubble to be moved away by the robotic arm of the space shuttle by a distance $D$ = 4.5 m, and mark the correct alternative.

Suppose that during this operation the space shuttle remained approximately in Uniform Rectilinear Motion (URM) and had infinite mass.

Hint: $D = \frac{1}{2} a t^2$, where $t$ is the time.

( ) $a_H = 0.001\ \text{m/s}^2$ and $t = 30$ s
( ) $a_H = 0.002\ \text{m/s}^2$ and $t = 900$ s
( ) $a_H = 0.004\ \text{m/s}^2$ and $t = 90$ s
( ) $a_H = 0.0001\ \text{m/s}^2$ and $t = 300$ s

No dia 24 de abril de 2020 o Telescópio Espacial Hubble completou 30 anos em órbita da Terra. Seu planejamento começou ainda nos anos 1970, mas ele só foi lançado em 1990. Ao receberem as primeiras imagens os cientistas ficaram perplexos com a má qualidade delas. Após algumas análises, eles descobriram que o Hubble possuía uma falha no espelho principal. Os engenheiros da NASA decidiram que os astronautas poderiam capturar o Hubble com o braço robótico do ônibus espacial e por meio de atividades extra veiculares consertar seu sistema óptico. Depois dos reparos o Hubble foi colocado de volta à sua órbita original. Essa missão de reparo do Hubble consistiu em um dos maiores feitos da NASA e, desde então, 4 outras missões de manutenção foram realizadas. (A figura rotula o Telescópio Hubble, o braço robótico e o Ônibus Espacial.)

Pergunta 15) Suponha que para recolocar o Hubble em sua órbita correta, o braço robótico do ônibus espacial exerceu 1 N de força ($F$), cujo módulo, direção e sentido foram constantes durante toda a manobra e perpendicular à direção do movimento do ônibus espacial. A massa do Hubble ($m_H$) é de, aproximadamente, 10.000 kg. A segunda Lei de Newton diz que $F = ma$ ($m$ = massa e $a$ = aceleração).

Suponha que durante esta operação o ônibus espacial manteve-se aproximadamente em Movimento Retilíneo Uniforme (MRU) e tinha massa infinita.

Dica: $D = \frac{1}{2} a t^2$, onde $t$ é o tempo.

The company Visiona Tecnologia Espacial S.A., of São José dos Campos, SP, is developing the VCUB nanosatellite, with a mass of 10 kg. The satellite orbits at an altitude of 500 km, its orbital period is 1.5 h and it "sweeps" a strip of 250 km of the Earth's surface.

Do the calculations of $H$ (part A), $D$ (part B) and $N$ (part C) and mark the answer that contains the correct values of $H$, $D$, $N$.

Question 17a) Suppose that a certain point $A$ fixed on the Equator line is exactly at the centre of the strip "swept" by the sensor of the VCUB when it crosses the plane of the Equator. Consider this instant as time $t$ = 0 s. The statement of the question gave the period of the satellite, that is, how long it takes to complete one revolution around the Earth. Therefore, as the VCUB revolves in a plane perpendicular to the plane of the Equator, the Earth also rotates about its axis of rotation. The orbital plane of the VCUB does not change, but the surface of the Earth rotates under it. Thus, on completing one orbit and crossing the plane of the Equator again, coming from North to South, the camera of the VCUB will no longer be over point $A$, since it moved along with the Earth's surface.

Calculate the distance $H$ (in km), indicated in the figure, by which point $A$ moved away from its initial position when the VCUB crosses the plane of the Equator again.

Question 17b) Calculate the distance $D$ (in km), indicated in the figure of the previous item, measured along the Equator line, that the VCUB failed to monitor between two consecutive passes.

So that after the first satellite (VCUB 1) crosses the plane of the Equator, another satellite (VCUB 2), in the same orbit as the first and right behind it, crosses the plane of the Equator some time later, covering the next 250 km, and so on for VCUB 3, VCUB 4 etc., until VCUB 1 crosses the plane of the Equator again.

Thus, on completing one orbit and crossing the plane of the Equator again, coming from North to South, the camera of the VCUB will no longer be over point $A$, since it moved along with the Earth's surface.

O principal objetivo do VCUB é obter imagens da superfície terrestre (sensoriamento remoto). Conforme mostrado na figura, o plano de órbita do satélite é perpendicular ao plano equatorial terrestre. O satélite orbita a 1000 km de altitude, seu período orbital é de 1,8 h e ele "varre" uma faixa de 300 km da superfície da Terra.

Realize os cálculos de $H$ (parte A), $D$ (parte B) e $N$ (parte C) e assinale a resposta que contém os valores corretos de $H$, $D$, $N$.

Considere este instante como sendo tempo $t$ = 0 s. No enunciado da questão foi dado o período do satélite, ou seja, quanto tempo ele leva para completar um giro em torno da Terra. Logo, na medida em que o VCUB gira em um plano perpendicular ao plano do Equador, a Terra também gira em torno do seu eixo de rotação. O plano da órbita do VCUB não muda, mas a superfície da Terra gira sob ele. Assim, ao completar uma órbita e passar novamente pelo plano do Equador, vindo do Norte para o Sul, a câmera do VCUB não estará mais sobre o ponto $A$, pois este se deslocou junto com a superfície da Terra.

Calcule a distância $H$ (em km), indicada na figura, que o ponto $A$ se afastou da sua posição inicial quando o VCUB cruzar o plano do Equador novamente.

Pergunta 18b) Calcule a distância $D$ (em km), indicada na figura do item anterior, medida ao longo da linha do Equador, que o VCUB deixou de monitorar entre duas passagens consecutivas.

De forma que depois que o primeiro satélite (VCUB 1) cruzar o plano do Equador, outro satélite (VCUB 2), na mesma órbita que o primeiro e logo atrás dele, cruze o plano do Equador um tempo depois, cobrindo os próximos 300 km e assim sucessivamente para os VCUB 3, VCUB 4 etc., até o VCUB 1 voltar a cruzar o plano do Equador novamente.

Calcule quantos ($N$) VCUBs serão necessários para cobrir toda a distância $D$ numa única passagem completa desta constelação.

problems.problem:
The spatial resolution of a satellite sensor is defined as the capacity that the sensor has to discriminate objects according to their size, that is, the level of detail with which we can observe objects on the Earth's surface. If a satellite has a spatial resolution of 30 m, this means that areas of dimensions smaller than 30 m $\times$ 30 m cannot be identified. There are low-resolution satellites (50 m, used for monitoring large regions, such as forests) and high-resolution satellites (0.5 m, capable of identifying cars and machines on the surface of the Earth).

Do Part A and Part B and mark the alternative that contains the correct values of what is asked.

Part A) The image sensor of digital cameras is made of tiny light-sensitive elements called pixels. The following images give an example of how the same car can be seen with different spatial resolutions. Each little square of each of the images corresponds to 1 pixel of the image. The more pixels an image has, the better the resolution of the image. (The four images are labelled 1.60 m, 0.80 m, 0.40 m and 0.20 m.)

Suppose that the image of the VCUB camera is composed of 4000 $\times$ 4000 pixels, whose spatial resolution is 3 m, that is, each pixel of the image corresponds to an area of 3 m $\times$ 3 m (= 9 m$^2$) on the surface of the Earth.
Knowing this, calculate the total area $A$ (in km$^2$) represented by each image of the VCUB.

Part B) Invaders of indigenous lands deforested, in one day, an area of 90 m $\times$ 90 m (almost 1 hectare!). Considering the absence of clouds, calculate the number ($N$) of pixels that the image of the deforested area will occupy on the sensor of the VCUB.

( ) $A$ = 144000 km$^2$ and $N$ = 800 pixels
( ) $A$ = 144 km$^2$ and $N$ = 900 pixels
( ) $A$ = 144000000 km$^2$ and $N$ = 400 pixels
( ) $A$ = 16000000 km$^2$ and $N$ = 810 pixels
( ) $A$ = 9 km$^2$ and $N$ = 900 pixels

( ) $A$ = 144 km$^2$ e $N$ = 900 pixels

problems.problem:
Voyager 2 is an American robotic spacecraft launched by NASA on 20 August 1977. The probe approached the four giant planets of the Solar System, producing extremely valuable scientific results and the best photographs of those bodies and of their satellites obtained until then. It became the fourth human artifact to go beyond the orbit of Pluto, in 1989, and at the end of 2005 it was at a distance of about 75 AU (astronomical units) from the Earth.
(Figure: Voyager 2. Image credit: NASA (public domain).)

Its current speed relative to the Sun is 15.3 km/s, which is equivalent to about 3.23 AU/year.

Mark the alternative that gives the distance, in AU, at which Voyager 2 was from the Earth at the end of 2015.

a) 107.3
b) 75.0
c) 104.7
d) 110.5
e) 91.1

problems.problem:
In astronomy, luminosity is the amount of energy that a body radiates in a unit of time. It is typically expressed in units of watts or in terms of the Solar luminosity, $L_{Sun} = 3.8\times10^{26}$ Watt. This energy is generated in the core of the Sun through nuclear fusion reactions. Part of the mass involved in the fusion is transformed into energy.

Mark the alternative that gives the approximate value of the solar mass (in kg) transformed into energy every minute.

b) $2.5\times10^{11}$
c) $1.3\times10^{18}$
d) $7.6\times10^{19}$
e) $4.2\times10^{15}$

problems.problem:
In 2021 NASA's rover Perseverance, with dimensions equivalent to those of a car, was placed on Mars to explore its surface and carry out a series of experiments.

b) 10
c) 30

problems.problem:
NASA's rover Perseverance, in order to land safely on the Martian surface in 2021, had to carry out a sequence of very risky aerospace manoeuvres. With a mass of 1025 kg, on reaching 120 km from the Martian surface, Perseverance began the process of entry (recorded as time = 0 s in the table below), descent and landing. Until the parachute was deployed the speed was reduced solely as a result of the friction between the capsule that protects Perseverance and the Martian atmosphere. Then the parachute was deployed and worked for 2 minutes, when it was ejected and 8 retrorockets came into operation, which reduced the final speed from 306 km/h to 3.6 km/h.

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Event} & \text{Time [s]} & \text{Altitude [km]} & \text{Speed [km/h]} & \text{Speed [m/s]} \\ \hline \text{Contact with the Martian atmosphere} & 0 & 120 & 19800 & 5500 \\ \hline \text{Parachute deployment} & 240 & 11 & 1512 & 420 \\ \hline \text{Parachute ejection and retrorocket ignition} & 360 & 2 & 306 & 85 \\ \hline \text{Ejection of the retrorocket system and landing} & 420 & 0.02 & 3.6 & 1 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Based on this information, mark the option that gives the approximate value of the deceleration of Perseverance due to the friction with the atmosphere.

a) $-21.2\ \text{m/s}^2$
b) $-2.8\ \text{m/s}^2$
c) $-1.4\ \text{m/s}^2$
d) $-76.2\ \text{m/s}^2$
e) $-10.1\ \text{m/s}^2$
problems.problem_orig:
O jipe-robô Perseverance, da NASA, para pousar em segurança na superfície marciana, em 2021, teve que realizar uma sequência de manobras aeroespaciais muito arriscadas. Com 1.025 kg de massa, ao chegar à 120 km da superfície marciana, o Perseverance iniciou o processo de entrada (registrado por tempo = 0 s na tabela abaixo), descida e pouso. Até o acionamento do paraquedas a velocidade foi reduzida tão-somente em função do atrito entre a cápsula que protege o Perseverance e a atmosfera marciana. Depois o paraquedas foi acionado e funcionou por 2 minutos, quando foi ejetado e entraram em funcionamento 8 retrofoguetes que reduziram a velocidade final de 306 km/h para 3,6 km/h.

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Evento} & \text{Tempo [s]} & \text{Altitude [km]} & \text{Velocidade [km/h]} & \text{Velocidade [m/s]} \\ \hline \text{Contato com a atmosfera marciana} & 0 & 120 & 19.800 & 5.500 \\ \hline \text{Acionamento do paraquedas} & 240 & 11 & 1.512 & 420 \\ \hline \text{Ejeção do paraquedas e acionamento dos retrofoguetes} & 360 & 2 & 306 & 85 \\ \hline \text{Ejeção do sistema de retrofoguetes e pouso} & 420 & 0{,}02 & 3{,}6 & 1 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Baseado nessas informações, assinale a opção que traz o valor aproximado da desaceleração do Perseverance devido ao atrito com a atmosfera.

a) $-21{,}2\ \text{m/s}^2$
b) $-2{,}8\ \text{m/s}^2$
c) $-1{,}4\ \text{m/s}^2$
d) $-76{,}2\ \text{m/s}^2$
e) $-10{,}1\ \text{m/s}^2$

problems.problem:
The mass of a star is the fuel for the nuclear fusion processes. We can therefore assume that its lifetime on the Main Sequence is proportional to the stellar mass divided by its Luminosity, which is a measure of its energy production.

Stellar evolution models tell us that only a fraction of the mass of a star is actually available as nuclear fuel. Using the Sun as a parameter and assuming that its life on the Main Sequence will be $10\times10^{9}$ years (10 billion years), the lifetime $T$ predicted for a star to remain on the Main Sequence will depend on its Mass $M$ according to the following formula:

$$T = 10^{10}\left(\frac{M_{Sun}}{M_{star}}\right)^{\frac{5}{2}}\ \text{years}$$

Using the formula, mark the alternative that gives the lifetime of the hypergiant star with 100 times the mass of the Sun ($M_{star} = 100\,M_{Sun}$).

a) 100000 years
b) 1000000 years
c) 10000000 years
d) 100000000 years
e) 1000000000 years

Os modelos de evolução estelar nos dizem que apenas uma fração da massa de uma estrela está realmente disponível como combustível nuclear. Utilizando o Sol como parâmetro e assumindo que sua vida na Sequência Principal será de $10\times10^{9}$ anos (10 bilhões de anos), o tempo de vida $T$ previsto para uma estrela permanecer na Sequência Principal dependerá de sua Massa $M$ de acordo com a seguinte fórmula:

$$T = 10^{10}\left(\frac{M_{Sol}}{M_{estrela}}\right)^{\frac{5}{2}}\ \text{anos}$$

Utilizando a fórmula, assinale a alternativa que traz o tempo de vida da estrela hiper gigante com 100 vezes a massa do Sol ($M_{estrela} = 100\,M_{Sol}$).

a) 100.000 anos
b) 1.000.000 anos
c) 10.000.000 anos
d) 100.000.000 anos
e) 1.000.000.000 anos

problems.problem:
Nicknamed "the biggest eye in the world turned to the sky", the Extremely Large Telescope, or just ELT, will be the largest optical telescope on the planet. Developed by the European Southern Observatory (ESO), to be installed in the Atacama Desert, in Chile, the instrument will have a mirror measuring 39 metres in diameter, with inauguration expected in 2027.

The largest telescope installed in Brazil is at the Pico dos Dias Observatory (OPD), in the city of Brazópolis/MG, and is managed by the National Astrophysics Laboratory (LNA/MCTI). Its primary mirror is 1.6 metres in diameter.

Consider that a digital camera, attached to the OPD telescope, needs 600 seconds of exposure to record the image of a certain very faint star.

Mark the option that gives the approximate time that the ELT will need to record this same star using this same digital camera attached to its mirror.

Hint: the light of the star is collected by the primary mirror of a telescope. So, the larger the area of the mirror, the more light the mirror collects and the faster the digital camera records its image.

a) 1.0 s
b) 1.6 s
c) 10.0 s
d) 24.0 s
e) 39.0 s

problems.problem:
Neptune is the eighth planet of the Solar System, the last one from the Sun since the reclassification of Pluto to the category of Dwarf Planet, in 2006. It belongs to the group of gas giants, with a mass equivalent to 17 Earth masses. Neptune orbits the Sun at a mean distance of 30.1 astronomical units. Neptune's orbit has an orbital period of approximately 164 Earth years and its eccentricity is only 0.011, which makes it one of the most circular orbits among the planets of the Solar System.

With respect to the perpendicular to the plane of its orbit, Neptune's rotation axis is tilted by $28.3^\circ$, similar to the tilt of the Earth's axis, which is $23.5^\circ$. Because of this the planet shows seasonal variations of the solar radiation received in the northern and southern hemispheres, just like the Earth.

In the year 2005 the summer solstice began in Neptune's Southern Hemisphere. Mark the option that gives the year in which the last winter solstice occurred in this same Hemisphere of Neptune.

a) 1923
b) 1841
c) 1964
d) 1882
e) 1800

problems.problem:
A sundial is a clock that tells the solar time from the projection of the shadow of a rod. In the strictest sense of the word, it consists of a flat plate (or dial) and a rod, which casts a shadow on the dial. As the Sun appears to move across the sky, the shadow lines up with the different hour lines, which are marked on the dial to indicate the true solar time.

On the right we have a vertical sundial (its dial stands upright), carved in stone, where we see its rod, in the shape of an arrow (the small arrow), and its shadow (the long arrow) marking the local solar time.

In the image on the right, we also see 3 lines highlighted with the letters A, B and C. Lines A and C mark, respectively, the limits of the minimum and maximum lengths that the shadow of the rod can reach throughout the year, that is, during the solstices. Line B corresponds to the equinoxes.

The installation of a sundial requires knowledge of the local latitude (because the rod has to be mounted so as to be parallel to the Earth's rotation axis), of the precise vertical direction (for example, by means of a level or plumb line) and of the direction of the Cardinal Points.

Based on the information in the text, mark the only true option.

a) During the Summer Solstice the tip of the shadow of the rod traces line C.
b) We read on the dial that it is 10 h in the morning.
c) This clock will show the true solar time at whatever latitude it is installed.
d) If this clock is placed horizontally, it will still show the solar time correctly.
e) This clock can be installed with its dial facing any Cardinal Point

[The photograph is not reproduced here (its author is not credited in the paper). It is on page 10 of the official paper: https://sistema.oba.org.br/sisglob/sisglob_arquivos/downloads/Prova%20nivel%204%20da%2025%20OBA%20DE%202022.pdf]
problems.problem_orig:
Um relógio de Sol é um relógio que marca a hora solar a partir da projeção da sombra de uma haste. No sentido mais restrito da palavra, consiste em uma placa plana (ou mostrador) e uma haste, que projeta uma sombra no mostrador. Conforme o Sol parece se mover no céu, a sombra se alinha com as diferentes linhas horárias, que são marcadas no mostrador para indicar a hora solar verdadeira.

À direita temos um relógio de Sol vertical (seu mostrador fica em pé), esculpido em pedra, onde vemos sua haste, em forma de seta (a seta pequena), e sua sombra (a seta longa) marcando a hora solar local.

Na imagem à direita, também vemos 3 linhas destacadas com as letras A, B e C. As linhas A e C demarcam, respectivamente, o limite dos comprimentos mínimo e máximo que a sombra da haste pode atingir ao longo do ano, ou seja, durante os solstícios. A linha B corresponde aos equinócios.

A instalação de um relógio de Sol requer o conhecimento da latitude local (pois a haste precisa ser montada de forma a ficar paralela ao eixo de rotação da Terra), da direção vertical precisa (por exemplo, através de um nível ou prumo) e da direção dos Pontos Cardeais.

Baseado nas informações do texto, assinale a única opção verdadeira.

a) Durante o Solstício de Verão a ponta da sombra da haste percorre a linha C.
b) Lemos no mostrador que são 10 h da manhã.
c) Este relógio vai marcar a hora solar verdadeira em qualquer latitude em for instalado.
d) Se este relógio for colocado na horizontal, ele continuará marcando a hora solar corretamente.
e) Este relógio pode ser instalado com seu mostrador virado de frente para qualquer Ponto Cardeal

[A fotografia não é reproduzida aqui (seu autor não é creditado na prova). Está na página 10 da prova oficial: https://sistema.oba.org.br/sisglob/sisglob_arquivos/downloads/Prova%20nivel%204%20da%2025%20OBA%20DE%202022.pdf]

problems.problem:
Black holes are so dense that enormous quantities of matter can be compressed into very small spaces. Since black holes are the result of a gravitational collapse, at least theoretically, there is no limit to how large or small they can be. The size of a black hole depends on something called the Schwarzschild Radius ($R_{Sch}$). This radius is associated with the extent of the event horizon that there would be if the mass of such a body were concentrated in a single point of infinitesimal dimensions.

The following table gives the theoretical radius of black holes of various masses. The masses are all given in terms of the mass of the Earth ($M_T = 6.00\times10^{24}$ kg), so that '2.0' means a black hole with twice the mass of our planet.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline M_T & R_{Sch}\ (\text{cm}) \\ \hline 1.0 & 0.88 \\ \hline 2.0 & 1.76 \\ \hline 3.2 & 2.82 \\ \hline 5.0 & 4.40 \\ \hline 7.5 & 6.60 \\ \hline 8.8 & 7.74 \\ \hline 11.0 & 9.68 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Next we have the values of the table plotted on a graph (horizontal axis: "Massa do Buraco Negro (Terra = 1,0)" = Black hole mass (Earth = 1.0), from 0 to 12; vertical axis: "Raio (cm)" = Radius (cm), from 0 to 12).

With the information from the table and from the graph, mark the option that gives the approximate theoretical value of the radius of a black hole with mass equivalent to the mass of Jupiter ($1.92\times10^{27}$ kg).

a) 2.82 m
b) 5.64 m
c) 1.92 m
d) 12.50 m
e) 14.10 m

Como os buracos negros são o resultado de um colapso gravitacional, pelo menos teoricamente, não há limite para quão grandes ou pequenos eles podem ser. O tamanho de um buraco negro depende de algo chamado Raio de Schwarzschild ($R_{Sch}$). problems.problem:
Without an atmosphere, there is nothing to stop millions of kg of rock and ice fragments, wandering through space, from hitting the lunar surface every year. On Earth, our atmosphere protects us and few fragments reach the ground. Travelling at about 19 km/s, these fragments are faster than a bullet and are totally silent and invisible until they hit the surface of the Moon. This is something that future lunar explorers and settlers need to worry about!

For 2 consecutive years, NASA astronomers counted 100 flashes of light from meteorite impacts on the lunar surface, each equivalent to a few tens of kg of TNT, hence the concern.

Consider that the astronomers were only able to observe the impacts on 1/4 of the surface of the Moon and that the Moon is spherical with radius $R_{Moon} = 1737.0$ km.

With this information, mark the option that gives the approximate time that a lunar colony of 10 km$^2$ must wait for a direct impact on its facilities to occur.

Hints: - use the formula $A = 4\pi R^2$ to calculate the area of the surface of the Moon;
- calculate the rate of impacts in terms of 'meteorites/km$^2$ year';
- multiply the rate above by the total area of the lunar colony. You will obtain a number much smaller than 1 meteorite per year falling on the area of the lunar base.
- Finally, calculate how long it will be necessary to wait for ONE meteorite to fall on the lunar base in question.

a) 19000 years
b) 76000 years
c) 9500 years
d) 1737 years
e) 2 years
problems.problem_orig:
Sem uma atmosfera, não há nada que impeça que milhões de kg de fragmentos de rocha e gelo, que vagam pelo espaço, atinjam a superfície lunar todo o ano. Na Terra, nossa atmosfera nos protege e poucos fragmentos chegam até o solo. Viajando a cerca de 19 km/s, estes fragmentos são mais rápidos que uma bala e são totalmente silenciosos e invisíveis até atingirem a superfície da Lua. Isso é algo com que os futuros exploradores e colonos lunares precisam se preocupar!

Durante 2 anos seguidos, os astrônomos da NASA contaram 100 flashes de luz provenientes dos impactos de meteoritos na superfície lunar, cada um equivalente a algumas dezenas de kg de TNT, por isso a preocupação.

Considere que os astrônomos só conseguiram observar os impactos em 1/4 da superfície da Lua e que a Lua é esférica com raio $R_{Lua} = 1.737{,}0$ km.

Com essas informações, assinale a opção que traz o tempo aproximado que uma colônia lunar de 10 km$^2$ deverá esperar para ocorrer um impacto direto em suas instalações.

Dicas: - utilize a fórmula $A = 4\pi R^2$ para calcular a área da superfície da Lua;
- calcule a taxa de impactos em termos de 'meteoritos/km$^2$ ano';
- multiplique a taxa acima pela área total da colônia lunar. Você obterá um número muito menor do que 1 meteorito por ano caindo na área da base lunar.
- Calcule, finalmente, quanto tempo será necessário esperar para que UM meteorito caia na base lunar em questão.

a) 19.000 anos
b) 76.000 anos
c) 9.500 anos
d) 1.737 anos
e) 2 anos

problems.problem:
At Christmas 2021, a masterpiece of space engineering was launched into space. It is the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), with a mass of 6000 kg, which took decades to develop and required investments of 10 billion US dollars from the USA, Europe and Canada. To position the JWST at the Lagrange point L2, located 1.5 million kilometres from the Earth (along the Earth-Moon line), the European rocket Ariane 5 was used, which has 3 stages, as illustrated in the figure. The 2 engines of the 1st stage of Ariane 5 use solid propellant and run for 2 minutes, after which they are released, falling into the sea. The engine of the 2nd stage runs for 9 minutes, at the end of which the stage is ejected and the engine of the 3rd stage is ignited. The latter runs for 16 minutes. The 2nd and 3rd stages use liquid propellant: hydrogen (fuel) and oxygen (oxidizer). The energy released during the chemical reaction between H$_2$ and O$_2$ generates water vapour at a temperature of 3000 $^\circ$C and a pressure of 100 atmospheres inside the combustion chamber. It is the expansion of these gases through the nozzle that generates the thrust force necessary for the motion of Ariane 5. (The figures show the Ariane 5 rocket with its JWST payload and the labelled 1st, 2nd and 3rd stages, and a diagram of a rocket engine with the labels Oxidante, Combustível, Tubeira and Câmara de combustão = Oxidizer, Fuel, Nozzle and Combustion chamber.)

$$2\,\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\,\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{ENERGY}$$

Item a) Consider that at the instant of launch the total mass of the Ariane 5 rocket is 800000 kg. What percentage of this total corresponds to the James Webb Space Telescope?

Item b) Considering that the electromagnetic waves sent by the JWST transmission system travel at the speed of light (300000 km/s), what is the time necessary for this information to arrive from the space telescope at the Earth?

Mark the alternative that contains the correct answers to items "a" and "b" above and in the correct sequence.

a) 0.75% and 5.0 s
b) 0.60 % and 3.0 s
c) 0.80% and 5.0 s
d) 0.75% and 3.0 s
e) 0.60% and 4.0 s

Trata-se do Telescópio Espacial James Webb (James Webb Space Telescope - JWST), com 6.000 kg de massa, que levou décadas para ser desenvolvido e demandou investimentos de 10 bilhões de dólares dos EUA, Europa e Canadá. Para posicionar o JWST no ponto de Lagrange L2, situado a 1,5 milhão de quilômetros da Terra (ao longo da linha Terra-Lua), foi utilizado o foguete europeu Ariane 5, que possui 3 estágios, conforme ilustrado na figura. Os 2 motores do 1º estágio do Ariane 5 utilizam propelente sólido e funcionam por 2 minutos, após os quais são liberados, caindo no mar. O motor do 2º estágio funciona por 9 minutos, findos os quais o estágio é ejetado e o motor do 3º estágio é acionado. Este funciona por 16 minutos. O 2º e 3º estágios fazem uso de propelente líquido: hidrogênio (combustível) e oxigênio (oxidante). $$2\,\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\,\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{ENERGIA}$$

a) 0,75% e 5,0 s
b) 0,60 % e 3,0 s
c) 0,80% e 5,0 s
d) 0,75% e 3,0 s
e) 0,60% e 4,0 s

On 13 January 2022, the satellite PION-Br1 was launched into orbit, developed by the Brazilian company PION Labs, formed by young engineers who in the past took part in the OBA and in the MOBFOG. The PION-Br1 has a mass of 250 g, equivalent to the mass of a smartphone, and dimensions that allow it to fit in the palm of your hand. Despite its small mass and dimensions, it incorporates important technologies for the development of Brazilian space engineering. During the 3 years in which it will remain in orbit, the PION-Br1 will make measurements of temperature, pressure and speed, which will be transmitted to amateur radio stations on Earth.

In this way, the PION-Br1 shared its trip into space with another 100 satellites from various countries. Based on this information, calculate the average specific cost per kilogram (R\$/kg) of the Falcon 9.

To launch them into space, one of the possibilities is to use the Brazilian rocket VLM (Microsatellite Launch Vehicle), currently under development by the Institute of Aeronautics and Space (IAE). Considering that the VLM will be able to place 150 kg into Earth orbit, how many VLM flights will be necessary? For simplicity, consider that the 50 satellites will be placed in the same orbit.

Mark the alternative that contains the correct answers to items "a" and "b" above and in the correct sequence.

a) R\$ 20000.00/kg and 1 VLM flight
b) R\$ 20000.00/kg and 2 VLM flights
c) R\$ 3000000.00/kg and 1 VLM flight

e) R\$ 100000.00 and 1 VLM flight

O PION-Br1 possui 250 g, equivalente à massa de um smartphone, e dimensões que permitem que ele caiba na palma de sua mão. Apesar de sua pequena massa e dimensões, ele incorpora tecnologias importantes para o desenvolvimento da engenharia espacial brasileira. Durante os 3 anos em que permanecerá em órbita, o PION-Br1 efetuará medições de temperatura, pressão e velocidade, que serão transmitidas às estações de rádio amadores na Terra.

Item a) (0,5 ponto) O PION-Br1 foi lançado ao espaço pelo foguete americano Falcon 9, que tem capacidade para lançar 20.000 kg em órbita terrestre, ao custo de 300 milhões de reais. Dessa forma, o PION-Br1 compartilhou sua viagem ao espaço com outros 120 satélites de diversos países. Baseado nessas informações calcule o custo específico médio por quilograma (R\$/kg) do Falcon 9.

Item b) (0,5 ponto) A empresa PION Labs planeja estabelecer uma constelação de 75 satélites PION-Br1 em órbita terrestre. Para lança-los ao espaço, uma das possibilidades é usar o foguete brasileiro VLM (Veículo Lançador de Microssatélites), ora em desenvolvimento pelo Instituto de Aeronáutica e Espaço (IAE). Considerando que o VLM será capaz de colocar 150 kg em órbita terrestre, quantos voos do VLM serão necessários? Por simplicidade, considere que os 75 satélites serão colocados em uma mesma órbita.

Assinale a alternativa que contém as respostas corretas aos itens "a" e "b" acima e na sequência correta.

a) R\$ 15.000,00/kg e 1 voo do VLM
b) R\$ 15.000,00/kg e 2 voos do VLM
c) R\$ 2.500.000,00/kg e 1 voo do VLM
d) R\$ 2.500.000,00/kg e 2 voos do VLM
e) R\$ 120.000,00 e 1 voo do VLM

problems.problem:
On 18 February 2021, NASA landed the Perseverance rover and the small helicopter Ingenuity, illustrated in the figure, on Mars. To stay at a certain altitude in the Martian atmosphere the aerodynamic lift force ($S$), generated by the rotation of its set of blades, has to be equal to the weight force ($P = mg$). As the gravity on the Martian surface is lower than that on the Earth's surface, it seems to be easier to fly on Mars than on Earth. But it is not that simple. The force $S$ is proportional to the atmospheric density, which, near the Martian surface, is equivalent to 1% of that on the Earth's surface. To compensate for the low density, the set of blades of Ingenuity rotates at 2400 revolutions per minute (rpm). The energy needed to rotate the blades is supplied by batteries, fed by solar energy. In this context, Ingenuity is considered by NASA a technology demonstrator, that is, its objective is to show the possibility of flying in the rarefied atmosphere of the red planet. (The figure is a drawing of the helicopter, labelled "Painel solar" = solar panel, "Hélices" = blades and "Baterias" = batteries, with an arrow $S$ pointing up and an arrow $P$ pointing down.)

Hint: in your calculations take the acceleration of gravity $g$ on Mars to be 0.36 that on Earth.

Item a) Ingenuity has a mass $m$ = 1.8 kg. Calculate the aerodynamic lift force, $S$, necessary to keep it flying in a fixed position near the surface of Mars. Consider that the acceleration of gravity on the surface of the Earth is 10 m/s$^2$.

Item b) Using a simplified approach, the lift force acting on the blades is given by $S = C \times \rho \times v^2$, where $C$ is a constant, $\rho$ is the local atmospheric density and $v$ is the mean rotation speed of the blades. Considering that the rotation speed of the blades is the same on Mars and on Earth, calculate the ratio $S_{Earth}/S_{Mars}$.

Mark the alternative that contains the correct answers to items "a" and "b" above and in the correct sequence.

a) 6.48 N and 100
b) 3.60 N and 100
c) 6.48 N and 10
d) 3.60 N and 10
e) 8.00 N and 100

problems.problem_orig:
Em 18 de fevereiro de 2021, a NASA pousou em Marte o jipe-robô Perseverance e o pequeno helicóptero Ingenuity, ilustrado na figura. Para se manter em uma determinada altitude na atmosfera marciana a força aerodinâmica de sustentação ($S$), gerada pela rotação do seu conjunto de hélices, tem que ser igual à força peso ($P = mg$). Como a gravidade na superfície marciana é menor que aquela existente na superfície terrestre, parece ser mais fácil voar em Marte do que na Terra. Mas não é tão simples assim. A força $S$ é proporcional à densidade atmosférica, que, próximo à superfície marciana, equivale a 1% daquela existente na superfície terrestre. Para compensar a baixa densidade, o conjunto de hélices do Ingenuity gira a 2.400 rotações por minuto (rpm). A energia necessária para girar as hélices é fornecida por baterias, alimentadas por energia solar. Neste contexto, o Ingenuity é considerado pela NASA um demonstrador tecnológico, ou seja, seu objetivo é mostrar a possibilidade de voar na rarefeita atmosfera do planeta vermelho. (A figura é um desenho do helicóptero, rotulado "Painel solar", "Hélices" e "Baterias", com uma seta $S$ para cima e uma seta $P$ para baixo.)

Dica: em seus cálculos considere a aceleração da gravidade $g$ em Marte igual a 0,36 daquela existente na Terra.

Item a) O Ingenuity tem massa $m$ = 1,8 kg. Calcule a força aerodinâmica de sustentação, $S$, necessária para mantê-lo voando numa posição fixa próxima à superfície de Marte. Considere que a aceleração da gravidade na superfície da Terra seja de 10 m/s$^2$.

Item b) Usando uma abordagem simplificada, a força de sustentação que atua sobre as hélices é dada por $S = C \times \rho \times v^2$, onde $C$ é uma constante, $\rho$ é a densidade atmosférica local e $v$ é a velocidade média de rotação das hélices. Considerando que a velocidade de rotação das hélices é a mesma em Marte e na Terra, calcule a razão $S_{Terra}/S_{Marte}$.

Assinale a alternativa que contém as respostas corretas aos itens "a" e "b" acima e na sequência correta.

a) 6,48 N e 100
b) 3,60 N e 100
c) 6,48 N e 10
d) 3,60 N e 10
e) 8,00 N e 100

problems.problem:
The image below shows a photograph of Mount Fuji, Japan, on the day of the autumnal equinox, seen from the Keishin-in Monastery, a Buddhist school. On this day the Sun rises perfectly aligned with the summit of this famous volcano, which is still active.

The coordinates of Mount Fuji are: latitude $\phi = 35^\circ\,21'\,29''$ N and longitude $\lambda = 138^\circ\,43'\,52''$ E.

On the information given, FIRST write F (false) or T (true) in front of each statement and THEN choose the line that contains the correct sequence of F and T.

1st) One week after the autumnal equinox, the Sun will rise to the right of the summit of Mount Fuji.
2nd) One week after the autumnal equinox, the Sun will rise to the left of the summit of Mount Fuji.
3rd) This alignment occurs four times a year.
4th) At the spring equinox, the Sun also rises aligned with the summit of Mount Fuji.
5th) The summit of Mount Fuji and the monastery are aligned with the East-West direction.

Mark the alternative that contains the correct sequence of F and T.
a) 1st (T), 2nd (F), 3rd (F), 4th (T), 5th (T)
b) 1st (T), 2nd (F), 3rd (T), 4th (T), 5th (T)
c) 1st (T), 2nd (F), 3rd (T), 4th (F), 5th (T)
d) 1st (F), 2nd (T), 3rd (F), 4th (T), 5th (F)
e) 1st (F), 2nd (T), 3rd (T), 4th (F), 5th (F)

[The photograph is not reproduced here (it is a photograph by a private person). It is on page 1 of the official paper: https://sistema.oba.org.br/sisglob/sisglob_arquivos/downloads/Prova%20n%C3%ADvel%204%20da%2026%20OBA%20de%202023.pdf]

problems.problem:
When the Sun passes through the highest point of the sky, we say that true solar noon is occurring. When, on the following day, it passes again through this point, we say that 1 Solar Day has elapsed. If we use the stars as a reference, when a given star passes through the same place on the following day, we say that 1 Sidereal Day has elapsed.

The image below shows the scheme, not to scale, of the orbit of the Earth around the Sun at three distinct, consecutive moments: A, B and C.

On this image and based on your knowledge, mark the correct option.
a) Between moment A and moment C one Sidereal Day has elapsed.
b) Between moment A and moment B one Sidereal Day has elapsed.
c) Between moment A and moment B one Solar Day has elapsed.
d) Between moment A and moment B 24 hours have elapsed.
e) Between moment A and moment C 24 hours and 4 min have elapsed.

Quando, no dia seguinte, ele passa novamente por este ponto, dizemos que se passou 1 Dia Solar. Se usarmos as estrelas como referência, quando uma determinada estrela passa pelo mesmo lugar no dia seguinte, dizemos que se passou 1 Dia Sideral.

A imagem a seguir traz o esquema, fora de escala, da órbita da Terra em torno do Sol em três momentos distintos e consecutivos: A, B e C.

Sobre esta imagem e baseado nos seus conhecimentos, assinale a opção correta.
a) Entre o momento A e o momento C se passou um Dia Sideral.
b) Entre o momento A e o momento B se passou um Dia Sideral.
c) Entre o momento A e o momento B se passou um Dia Solar.
d) Entre o momento A e o momento B se passaram 24 horas.
e) Entre o momento A e o momento C se passaram 24 horas e 4 min.
