problems.problem:
One of the greatest novelties of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is its ability to find habitable exoplanets. This is because it carries on board a special instrument called NIRISS, capable of reading the chemical signature of distant places. To debut the instrument, the operators of James Webb pointed the telescope at the exoplanet WASP-96 b. It is one of more than 5000 that we know in the Milky Way, and is located 1150 light-years from us.

Located in the constellation Phoenix, it is a type of gas giant with a radius 1.2 times that of Jupiter, but with half of its mass. In addition, it is very hot. With an average temperature close to 500 °C, it is very close to its star, called WASP-96. Its orbit is so small that a complete year there lasts about 3.5 Earth days.

The image shows the graph of the light curve, the brightness of the star WASP-96, when the planet WASP-96 b passed across its disk, that is, during a planetary transit.

Based on the information presented and on the graph, FIRST write F (false) or T (true) in front of each statement and THEN choose the line that contains the correct sequence of F and T.

1st) During its transit, the planet WASP-96 b reduced the brightness of its star by 2%.
2nd) The maximum of the transit occurred at 16h on 21 June 2022.
3rd) In 1 Earth year, the planet WASP-96 b makes 100 revolutions around WASP-96.

The exploration of Mars is one of the most active areas of space research, with about 50 uncrewed missions to the red planet already carried out and/or planned, and there are even plans to take humans there in the near future. At this moment, there are two robotic rovers moving on the Martian surface (Curiosity and Perseverance), a small helicopter (Ingenuity) and seven satellites orbiting the red planet. Getting to Mars is an extraordinary challenge, which is why half of the missions sent there have failed. Imagine throwing a spacecraft the size of a car towards a point in space where Mars will be a few months from now. For this, rockets are used that are 60 m tall and have a mass of 531000 kg. That is right, to throw a 1000 kg spacecraft towards Mars, 480000 kg of propellant (fuel + oxidizer) are needed, which are consumed in only 20 minutes. During almost the whole trajectory to Mars, the gigantic rocket no longer exists. Small rocket engines of the spacecraft are used only for trajectory corrections and for landing on Mars. During this phase of unpowered flight, the spacecraft is under the almost exclusive influence of the gravitational field of the Sun.

Long before large rockets could be developed, the German scientist Walter Hohmann proposed, in 1925, an orbital transfer trajectory that involved the lowest propellant consumption, since then known as the Hohmann transfer orbit. In this trajectory (see figure) the perihelion of the transfer orbit lies on the orbit of the Earth, at point A, while the aphelion lies on the orbit of Mars, at point B. For the questions below, consider that the orbits of the Earth and Mars are circular and coplanar.

Item a) Knowing that the semi-major axis of an elliptical orbit around the Sun corresponds to half of the distance between the perihelion and the aphelion, calculate the value of the semi-major axis of the transfer orbit. Consider that the distance from the Earth to the Sun is 1.0 AU and that the distance between Mars and the Sun is 1.5 AU. Give the result in astronomical units (AU).

Item b) In 1619, the German Johannes Kepler proposed Kepler's Third Law, which says that the square of the period of an orbit divided by the cube of the semi-major axis of that orbit is constant for all bodies orbiting the same central body. For example, with $T$ the period and $S$ the semi-major axis of the transfer orbit, we have: $\dfrac{T^2}{S^3}=\dfrac{T_T^2}{R_T^3}$, where $T_T$ is the period of the orbit of the Earth, that is, 12 months, and $R_T$ is the distance from the Earth to the Sun, that is, 1.0 AU. Therefore, calculate the time for a spacecraft to travel from point A to B on the transfer orbit, in months. Remember that only half of the ellipse is traversed and that, for this reason, this time corresponds to half of the period of the transfer orbit. Consider $\sqrt{1.50}=1.22$ and $\sqrt{1.25}=1.12$.

b) 1.25 AU and 16.8 months
c) 1.22 AU and 22.0 months

Muito antes que os grandes foguetes pudessem ser desenvolvidos, o cientista alemão Walter Hohmann propôs, em 1925, uma trajetória de transferência orbital que envolvia o menor consumo de propelente, desde então conhecida como órbita de transferência de Hohmann. Seen from the Earth (E), the time elapsed for planets to return to the same configuration in the sky is known as the Synodic Period ($S$). In the scheme below, not to scale, at $t = 0$ we have Mars (M) in opposition. Because of the difference between the two orbital periods (the period of the Earth is shorter), a new opposition of Mars will only happen about 780 days after the first one.

The Synodic Period $S$ can be calculated by the following formula:

$$\frac{1}{S}=\frac{1}{P_1}-\frac{1}{P_2},$$

where $P_1$ and $P_2$ are the orbital periods of the planets in question, with $P_1 < P_2$.

In our example:

$$\frac{1}{S}=\frac{1}{P_{\text{Earth}}}-\frac{1}{P_{\text{Mars}}}=\frac{1}{365\ \text{days}}-\frac{1}{687\ \text{days}}\ \to\ S\cong 780\ \text{days}$$

Now consider an asteroid of the Main Asteroid Belt, located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, whose orbital period is 6 years.

Mark the option that gives the time interval between two consecutive oppositions of this asteroid.
a) 1.0 year.
b) 1.2 years.

d) 5.0 years.

problems.problem:
We know that the Luminosity ($L$) of stars is equivalent to the power of light bulbs and does not depend on their distance from us. When we plot a graph of Luminosity ($L$) against the surface Temperature ($T$) of stars we get what is known as the Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram, or simply the HR Diagram. It is a fundamental tool in astronomy to classify and understand stellar evolution. Stars are positioned in the HR diagram according to their surface temperature (horizontal axis) and their luminosity (vertical axis), revealing groups of stars known as the Main Sequence, White Dwarfs, Giants and Supergiants, as highlighted in the image.

The Sun, having a surface temperature $T = 6000$ K and solar luminosity $L = 1$, was positioned at the coordinates (6000, 1), being therefore classified as a Main Sequence star.

Position and classify three imaginary stars, E1, E2 and E3, according to their characteristics described below:

- E1 is ten thousand times more luminous than the Sun and its surface temperature is five times higher than that of the Sun;
- E2 has the same luminosity as E1 and its surface temperature is 4000 K;
- E3 has the same surface temperature as E2 and its luminosity is one hundred times smaller than that of the Sun.

Once the stars E1, E2 and E3 have been positioned in the HR Diagram, mark the only true option.
a) E2 is classified as a giant star.
b) E3 is classified as a white dwarf star.
c) E1 and E2 are classified as supergiant stars.
d) E1 and E3 are classified as Main Sequence stars.
e) E1, E2 and E3 are classified as Main Sequence stars.

Ele é uma ferramenta fundamental na astronomia para classificar e entender a evolução estelar. As estrelas são posicionadas no diagrama HR de acordo com sua temperatura superficial (eixo horizontal) e sua luminosidade (eixo vertical), revelando conjuntos estelares conhecidos como Sequência Principal, Anãs Brancas, Gigantes e Supergigantes, como em destaque na imagem.

problems.problem:
The SpaceX Starship rocket is composed of two stages. The first, called Super Heavy, has a total mass of 3600000 kg at the moment its 33 Raptor engines are fired. The second stage has a total mass of 1400000 kg ($M_2$) when the ignition of its 6 Raptor engines begins. The Starship intends to carry 100000 kg to Earth orbit and to reuse both its stages. In the test flight of November 2023, the 33 Raptor engines of the first stage operated for 2 minutes and 41 seconds, taking the rocket to an altitude of 70 km. At this instant the process of separation between the first and second stages begins. In this flight "hot staging" was used for the first time, which consists of firing the 6 engines of the second stage while it is still coupled to the first stage. In this way, the gases expelled by the engines of the second stage "push" the first stage downwards, as illustrated in the Figure next to this text by the force $\vec F$. From then on, the Thrust force $\vec E_2$, resulting from the firing of the 6 Raptor engines, will act on the second stage, besides the force of gravity. On the first stage, besides the force $\vec F$, the force of gravity and the thrust of only 3 of the 33 Raptor engines will act, which continue to operate to control its return to the Earth's surface. Because of the altitude at which the separation occurs, aerodynamic forces were considered negligible. Consider $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$.

Questions:

8a) Use Newton's Second Law to calculate the acceleration $a_2$ of the second stage at the instant of separation. For this, consider that the thrust force of the 6 Raptor engines is $E_2 = 1.4 \times 10^7\ \mathrm{N}$.

8b) Calculate the acceleration of the first stage assuming that, at the moment of separation, the first stage has a total mass $M_1 = 700000$ kg and 3 active Raptor engines, corresponding to a thrust force $E_1 = 7.0 \times 10^6\ \mathrm{N}$. Also consider that the force $F$ of the gases on the engine of the first stage is about 80% of the thrust force of the second stage, that is, $F = 1.12 \times 10^7\ \mathrm{N}$.

8c) Calculate the relative acceleration $a_{rel} = a_2 - a_1$ at the instant of the start of the separation.

Mark the alternative that contains the answers to items "8a", "8b" and "8c" above, in this order.
a) 10 m/s², 10 m/s², 10 m/s².
b) 5 m/s², -16 m/s², 0 m/s².
c) 0 m/s², -16 m/s², 16 m/s².
d) 0 m/s², 10 m/s², 16 m/s².
e) -5 m/s², -10 m/s², -10 m/s².

problems.problem:
Since the beginning of the Space Age in 1957, humanity has already sent hundreds of uncrewed spacecraft to explore the solar system. Currently, there are two of them in orbit around the Sun: the American Parker and the European Solar Orbiter. The Parker Probe was launched into space on 12 August 2018, by the Delta 4 Heavy rocket (Point 1 of the Figure), entering solar orbit on 19 January 2019. When passing by the planet Venus (Point 2 of the Figure), the Parker probe performed its first gravity-assist maneuver ("fly by"), the subject of a question of the OBA in 2018. As a result of this maneuver, Parker had its speed increased and its perihelion (minimum distance to the Sun) decreased. Over its 7 years of operation, the Parker Probe will make 24 orbits around the Sun with 7 close passes by Venus. At the end of this process, its perihelion will be reduced to 6 million kilometres. At its last perihelion, Parker will become the fastest man-made object. In this simplified exercise, we will calculate the value of this speed. For this, consider one of the elliptical orbits that the Parker Probe describes around the Sun. In this orbit, the principle of conservation of energy holds, with the sum of the kinetic energy $E_{cin}$ and the potential energy $E_{pot}$ being equal to the mechanical energy ($E_{mec}$): $E_{cin} + E_{pot} = E_{mec}$

Questions:

9a) Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the Parker Probe at the perihelion of its last orbit. For this, use the formula $E_{pot} = \dfrac{-m_S \times M \times G}{d}$, where $m_S = 600$ kg, corresponding to the mass of Parker, $M$ is the mass of the Sun and $G$ is the universal gravitational constant. $d$ is the smallest perihelion of all the orbits. To simplify your calculations, consider $M \times G = 1.27 \times 10^{20}\ \mathrm{m^3/s^2}$.

9b) Calculate the speed of the Parker Probe at the smallest perihelion of all the orbits. For this, consider $E_{mec} = -7 \times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{J}$ and $E_{pot}$ calculated in item 9a.

Hint: $E_{cin} = \dfrac{m_s \times V^2}{2}$, where $V$ is the magnitude of the speed.

Mark the alternative that contains the answers to items "9a" and "9b" above, in this order.
a) $1.00\times10^{13}$ J and 200 km/s.
b) $1.27\times10^{13}$ J and 100 km/s.
c) $2.54\times10^{13}$ J and 300 km/s.
d) $1.27\times10^{13}$ J and 200 km/s.
e) $1.00\times10^{13}$ J and 100 km/s.

Desde o início da Era Espacial em 1957, a humanidade já enviou centenas de espaçonaves não tripuladas para explorar o sistema solar. Atualmente, existem duas delas em órbita do Sol. A norte-americana Parker e a europeia Solar Orbiter. A Sonda Parker foi lançada ao espaço em 12 de agosto de 2018, pelo foguete Delta 4 Heavy (Ponto 1 da Figura), ingressando em órbita solar em 19 de janeiro de 2019. Ao passar pelo planeta Vênus (Ponto 2 da Figura), a sonda Parker realizou sua primeira manobra assistida por gravidade ("fly by"), tema de uma questão da OBA em 2018. Como resultado dessa manobra, a Parker teve sua velocidade aumentada e seu periélio (distância mínima ao Sol) diminuído. Ao longo de seus 7 anos de operação, a Sonda Parker realizará 24 órbitas ao redor do Sol com 7 passagens próximas de Vênus. Ao final desse processo, seu periélio será reduzido para 6 milhões de quilômetros. Em seu último periélio, a Parker tornar-se-á o objeto mais rápido feito pelo homem. Neste exercício simplificado, calcularemos o valor dessa velocidade. Para tanto, considere uma das órbitas elípticas que a Sonda Parker descreve ao redor do Sol. Nessa órbita, tem-se que vale o princípio da conservação da energia, com a soma da energia cinética $E_{cin}$ e energia potencial $E_{pot}$ sendo igual à energia mecânica ($E_{mec}$): $E_{cin} + E_{pot} = E_{mec}$

Perguntas:

9a) Calcule a energia potencial gravitacional da Sonda Parker no periélio de sua última órbita. Para isso, utilize a fórmula $E_{pot} = \dfrac{-m_S \times M \times G}{d}$, onde $m_S = 600$ kg, correspondente à massa da Parker, $M$ é a massa do Sol e $G$ é a constante da gravitação universal. $d$ é o menor periélio de todas as órbitas. Para simplificar seus cálculos, considere $M \times G = 1{,}27 \times 10^{20}\ \mathrm{m^3/s^2}$.

9b) Calcule a velocidade da Sonda Parker no menor periélio de todas as órbitas. Para isso, considere $E_{mec} = -7 \times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{J}$ e $E_{pot}$ calculada no item 9a.

Dica: $E_{cin} = \dfrac{m_s \times V^2}{2}$, onde $V$ é o módulo da velocidade.

Assinale a alternativa que contém as respostas aos itens "9a" e "9b" acima, nesta ordem.
a) $1{,}00\times10^{13}$ J e 200 km/s.
b) $1{,}27\times10^{13}$ J e 100 km/s.
c) $2{,}54\times10^{13}$ J e 300 km/s.

Kepler's Third Law states that the square of the period $P$ of revolution of a planet of mass $m$ around the Sun is directly proportional to the cube of its distance $r$ from the planet to the Sun, according to the equation:

$$P^2=\frac{4\pi^2}{G\left(M_{Sun}+m_{planet}\right)}\,r^3$$

Since the mass of any planet of the Solar System is much smaller than the mass of the Sun ($m_{planet} \ll M_{Sun}$), it can be neglected in the equation. Moreover, if the period $P$ is measured in Earth years and the distance $r$ to the Sun is measured in Astronomical Units (AU), which is the mean distance from the Earth to the Sun, then this equation becomes simply:

$$P^2=r^3$$

problems.problem:
In Astronomy, we call Synodic Period ($S$) the time that a celestial body takes to return to the same position relative to the Sun, as seen from the Earth. In other words, it is the time between two consecutive equal configurations of an astronomical object with respect to the Sun and the Earth and can be calculated by the following formula:

$$\frac{1}{S}=\frac{1}{P_1}-\frac{1}{P_2},$$

where $P_1$ and $P_2$ are the orbital periods of the bodies involved, with $P_1 < P_2$, so that the calculation results in a positive value. For example, the orbital period of the Moon around the Earth is approximately 27 days. Therefore, to have two consecutive Full Moons, we must wait, approximately:

$$\frac{1}{S_{Moon}}=\frac{1}{27\ \text{days}}-\frac{1}{365\ \text{days}}\ \to\ S_{Moon}\cong 29\ \text{days}$$

In December 2024, Mars began to show its retrograde motion in the sky, that is, Mars, which in general moves eastward when observed relative to the stars, starts to move westward for a few months and then goes back to moving eastward, forming a "loop" in the sky. The Sun-Earth-Mars configuration that leads to retrograde motion repeats periodically. In the image next to this text we can see a photomontage of Mars, from a few years ago, showing this effect.

Given that Mars orbits the Sun once every 687 days (or 1.88 Earth years), approximately, on which of these dates (month and year) do you expect Mars to begin its retrograde motion again?
a) December 2025.
b) May 2026.
c) October 2026.
d) December 2026.
e) January 2027.

$$\frac{1}{S}=\frac{1}{P_1}-\frac{1}{P_2},$$

Onde $P_1$ e $P_2$ são os períodos orbitais entre os astros envolvidos, sendo $P_1 < P_2$, para a conta resultar num valor positivo. Por exemplo, o período orbital da Lua em torno da Terra é de, aproximadamente, 27 dias. Portanto, para termos duas Luas Cheias consecutivas, devemos esperar, aproximadamente:

problems.problem:
The most fundamental astronomical unit of time is the day, measured in terms of the rotation of the Earth. There is, however, more than one way to define the day. We normally think of it as the period of rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun, called the SOLAR DAY. After all, for most people, sunrise is more important than the rising time of Betelgeuse (Alpha Orionis) or of some other star. However, astronomers also use the SIDEREAL DAY, which is defined in terms of the period of rotation of the Earth relative to very distant stars, supposedly fixed on the Celestial Sphere.

A solar day, defined as lasting 24 hours, is slightly longer than a sidereal day because the Earth not only rotates, but also moves along its orbit around the Sun in one day.

The geometry of this system can be seen in the following figure, not to scale.

The Earth makes a $360^\circ$ turn around the Sun in about 365 days, therefore, it covers: $\dfrac{360\ \text{degrees}}{365\ \text{days}}\approx 1\ \dfrac{\text{degree}}{\text{day}}$

Thus, for the Sun to pass through its local meridian twice in a row, which represents the "Solar Day", the Earth has to rotate 361 degrees about its rotation axis.

In summary: 1 solar day (24 h = 1440 min) corresponds to $361^\circ$ and a sidereal day corresponds to $360^\circ$.

Using the "rule of three", we have:
$$\frac{1440\ \text{min}}{x\ \text{min}}=\frac{361^\circ}{360^\circ}\ \to\ x\cong 1436\ \text{min}\cong \text{sidereal day}$$

Therefore, the solar day (1440 min) is longer than the sidereal day (1436 min) by 4 minutes (1440 min - 1436 min = 4 min). Thus, the SIDEREAL DAY is about 4 minutes shorter than the SOLAR DAY and every star rises 4 min earlier each day.

Suppose that on a certain night you see, from your window, the star Canopus (the brightest star of the constellation Carina and the second brightest star in the night sky) rising from behind a building at 23h.

Mark the option that gives the rising time of Canopus after 45 days.
a) 0h.
b) 2h.
c) 19h.
d) 20h.
e) 23h.

problems.problem_orig:
A unidade astronômica mais fundamental de tempo é o dia, medido em termos da rotação da Terra. Há, no entanto, mais de uma maneira de definir o dia. Normalmente, pensamos nele como o período de rotação da Terra em relação ao Sol, chamado de DIA SOLAR. Afinal, para a maioria das pessoas, o nascer do Sol é mais importante do que o horário do nascer de Betelgeuse (Alpha Orionis) ou de alguma outra estrela. No entanto, os astrônomos também usam o DIA SIDERAL, que é definido em termos do período de rotação da Terra em relação às estrelas muito distantes, supostamente fixas na Esfera Celeste.

Um dia solar, definido como tendo 24 horas de duração, é um pouco mais longo do que um dia sideral porque a Terra não apenas gira, mas também se move ao longo da sua órbita ao redor do Sol em um dia.

A geometria deste sistema pode ser vista na figura a seguir, fora de escala.

A Terra dá uma volta de $360^\circ$ torno do Sol em cerca de 365 dias, logo, ela percorre: $\dfrac{360\ \text{graus}}{365\ \text{dias}}\approx 1\ \dfrac{\text{grau}}{\text{dia}}$

Sendo assim, para que o Sol passe pelo seu meridiano local duas vezes consecutivas, que representa o "Dia Solar", a Terra tem que girar 361 graus sobre seu eixo de rotação.

Resumindo: 1 dia solar (24h = 1.440 min) corresponde a $361^\circ$ e um dia sideral corresponde a $360^\circ$.

Usando a "regra de três", temos:
$$\frac{1440\ \text{min}}{x\ \text{min}}=\frac{361^\circ}{360^\circ}\ \to\ x\cong 1.436\ \text{min}\cong \text{dia sideral}$$

Logo, o dia solar (1.440 min) é maior do que o dia sideral (1.436 min) em 4 minutos (1.440 min -1.436 min = 4 min). Portanto, o DIA SIDERAL é cerca de 4 minutos mais curto do que o DIA SOLAR e toda estrela nasce 4 min mais cedo a cada dia.

Suponha que numa determinada noite você veja, da sua janela, a estrela Canopus (a estrela mais brilhante da constelação de Carina e a segunda estrela mais brilhante no céu noturno) nascendo por detrás de um prédio às 23h.

Assinale a opção que traz a hora de nascimento de Canopus depois de 45 dias.
a) 0h.
b) 2h.
c) 19h.
d) 20h.
e) 23h.

problems.problem:
The Santos-Dumont Crater, named in honour of the Brazilian inventor Alberto Santos-Dumont (1873 - 1932), a pioneer of aviation, is a small lunar impact crater with a diameter ($D$) of 8.1 km, located on the eastern edge of Mare Imbrium, approximately 54 km from the landing site of the Apollo 15 mission.

Imagine that the back of your eye works like the screen of a cell phone full of "pixels", which are small light-sensitive cells. What we call resolution is our ability to see two nearby points as separate objects instead of a single point. That is, if two objects are very close together, their light hits the same receptor cell, making our brain think they are one thing. In angular terms, if two points are less than 1 arcminute ($\theta = 1' = 1^\circ/60$) apart they are seen as one. This is why, from the backyard of your house, without a telescope, you cannot see the Santos-Dumont crater.

Now, consider the crew of Artemis II approaching the Moon and an astronaut looking at the Moon through the hatch.

Mark the option that gives the minimum distance, $S$, that the capsule would need to be from the surface of the Moon for the Santos-Dumont crater to be distinguishable as something more than a simple point.

Hint: use the small-angle approximation, which relates the linear size of an object (in this case, the diameter $D$ of the crater), the distance to it ($S$) and its angular size ($\theta$): $D = S \times \theta$ (where $\theta$ is measured in radians). Given: 1 arcminute ($1'$) $= 3 \times 10^{-4}$ radians.

Mark the correct option.
a) 30000 km.
b) 27000 km.
c) 8100 km.
d) 19050 km.
e) 81000 km.

problems.problem:
Sunspots are areas on the solar photosphere with temperatures lower than their surroundings due to intense local magnetic fields. This magnetism hinders the convection process, making it difficult for internal heat to rise and producing regions of approximately 3800 °C. Because they emit less light than the ordinary surface, which reaches 5500 °C, they appear as dark spots by pure visual contrast.

Over the years, astronomers noticed that the number of sunspots reached a maximum number (solar maximum), then after some time this number decreased until they disappeared completely from the surface of the Sun (solar minimum), and then appeared again and grew in number. This phenomenon was called the Solar Cycle and lasts, on average, 11 years.

Monitoring solar cycles is essential to predict space weather and protect terrestrial technological infrastructure. During solar maximum, flares can damage satellite components, interrupt GPS signals and overload electric power grids. In addition, this monitoring ensures the safety of astronauts, allowing missions to be planned outside periods of critical solar radiation emission.

The graph below shows in detail the sunspot count of the last 5 Solar Cycles, from Solar Cycle 21 to the current Solar Cycle 25. The small bar at the bottom of the graph shows all the complete solar cycles, from Solar Cycle 1 to Solar Cycle 25, and we can see that the sunspot count is not constant over the cycles, there being cycles with many spots ("strong" cycles) and cycles with few spots ("weak" cycles).

Based on the information contained in the graph, evaluate the following statements and then mark the correct option. (Image: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, adapted.)

I. If Solar Cycle 25 has a period of exactly 11 years and if it began at the beginning of 2020, then the next Solar Maximum will occur only in 2031;
II. The graph shows that the Sun necessarily alternates between a "strong" cycle and a "weak" cycle every 22 years;
III. Analysing Solar Cycle 24, it is observed that the rise time (from minimum to maximum) was shorter than the decline time (from maximum to minimum);
IV. Of the monitored cycles, shown in the small bar at the bottom of the graph, Solar Cycles 5 and 6 were the "weakest";
V. The Sun has been monitored for its number of sunspots since before the year 1800.

Mark the correct option.
a) Only I and II are incorrect.
b) Only I is incorrect.
c) II, IV and V are correct.
d) Only III and V are correct.
e) All are correct.

problems.problem_orig:
As manchas solares são áreas na fotosfera solar com temperaturas inferiores ao seu entorno devido a intensos campos magnéticos locais. Esse magnetismo impede o processo de convecção, dificultando a subida do calor interno e gerando regiões de aproximadamente 3.800 °C. Por emitirem menos luz que a superfície comum, que atinge 5.500 °C, elas aparecem como pontos escuros por puro contraste visual.

Ao longo dos anos, os astrônomos perceberam que o número de manchas solares atingia um número máximo (máximo solar), depois de um tempo esse número ia diminuindo até desaparecerem completamente da superfície do Sol (mínimo solar), para depois voltarem a aparecer e crescer em número. Este fenômeno foi chamado de Ciclo Solar e tem, em média, a duração de 11 anos.

Monitorar os ciclos solares é fundamental para prever o clima espacial e proteger a infraestrutura tecnológica terrestre. Durante o máximo solar explosões podem danificar componentes de satélites, interromper sinais de GPS e sobrecarregar redes de energia elétrica. Além disso, esse acompanhamento garante a segurança de astronautas, permitindo planejar missões fora de períodos de emissão de radiação solar crítica.

O gráfico a seguir traz em detalhe a contagem de manchas solares dos últimos 5 Ciclos Solares, do Ciclo Solar 21 ao atual Ciclo Solar 25. A pequena barra na parte inferior do gráfico mostra todos os ciclos solares completos, desde o Ciclo Solar 1 até o Ciclo Solar 25 e podemos ver que a contagem de manchas não é constante ao longo dos ciclos, podendo ter ciclos com muitas manchas (ciclos "fortes") e ciclos com poucas manchas (ciclos "fracos").

Baseado nas informações contidas no gráfico, avalie as seguintes afirmações e depois assinale a opção correta. (Imagem: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (adaptada).)

III. Analisando-se o Ciclo Solar 24, observa-se que o tempo de subida (do mínimo ao máximo) foi menor do que o tempo de declínio (do máximo ao mínimo);
IV. Dos ciclos monitorados, mostrados na pequena barra na parte inferior do gráfico, os Ciclos Solares 5 e 6 foram os mais "fracos";
V. O Sol tem sido monitorado quanto ao número de manchas desde antes do ano de 1800.

Assinale a opção correta.
a) Apenas I e II estão incorretas.
b) Apenas a I está incorreta.
c) II, IV e V estão corretas.
d) Apenas III e V estão corretas.

O Satélite de pesquisa de exoplanetas em trânsito, TESS (sigla em inglês), identificou um sistema estelar que consiste em seis estrelas, que fica a aproximadamente 1.900 anos-luz da Terra, na constelação de Eridanus. A descoberta foi anunciada em janeiro de 2021.

TIC 168789840, também conhecido como TYC 7037-89-1, é um sistema estelar com três pares de estrelas binárias: o Sistema A, com período orbital de 1,3 dia, o Sistema B, com período orbital de 8,2 dias e o Sistema C, com período orbital de 1,6 dia. Os Sistemas A e C, por sua vez, orbitam em torno de um centro de massa comum, formando o Sistema A+C, com período orbital de 4 anos. E este Sistema A+C orbita um centro de massa comum com o Sistema B, formando o Sistema A+C+B, com um período orbital de 2.000 anos. A imagem a seguir, fora de escala, traz esta espetacular configuração orbital. Atenção: Baseado nas informações contidas no texto e na imagem, PRIMEIRO coloque C, de certo, ou E, de errado, na frente de cada afirmação abaixo e, DEPOIS, assinale a alternativa que contém a sequência correta de C e E.

1ª) O Sistema B orbita o centro de massa comum do Sistemas A+C.
2ª) No tempo exato em que o Sistema B (mais lento) completa 10 órbitas em torno de seu próprio centro de massa, o Sistema C (mais rápido) terá completado mais de 50 órbitas completas.
3ª) Considerando um ano terrestre padrão de 365 dias, o par de estrelas do Sistema A realiza menos de 1.000 voltas completas entre si durante o tempo necessário para que o conjunto A+C complete uma única volta de 4 anos.
4ª) Supondo que a massa total do conjunto A+C seja aproximadamente igual à massa do Sistema B, se a distância média entre os centros de massa de A+C e de B fosse quadruplicada, o novo período orbital dessa órbita externa passaria a ser de aproximadamente 8 mil anos.
5ª) O período orbital do conjunto completo (Sistema A+C+B) é 500 vezes maior do que o período orbital da Sistema A+C.

problems.problem:
The Artemis II mission, which took the crew to orbit the Moon, did not have a single rocket, but three rockets combined in the first stage. The assembly was named the Space Launch System (SLS).

The SLS rocket of the Artemis II Mission uses two different types of propulsion at liftoff. First: on the sides, there are the two Solid Rocket Boosters (SRBs). These rockets are similar to the solid-propellant rockets of the OBAFOG, which once ignited only shut down when the propellant runs out. Second: in the center are the liquid-fuel RS-25 Engines. These engines are versatile, since they are like the accelerator of a car, that is, you can accelerate by "pressing harder" on the pedal or decelerate by "easing off the foot", or even "take the foot off".

Attention: Based on the information contained in the text and on your knowledge, FIRST write C (correct) or W (wrong) in front of each statement below and THEN mark the alternative that contains the correct sequence of C and W.

1st) The liquid-fuel engines (RS-25) provide most of the thrust at liftoff, and it is impossible to shut them down after ignition.
2nd) The solid-fuel rockets (SRBs) are known for their high efficiency and for the ease of controlling the thrust power during flight, allowing the rocket to accelerate or decelerate as needed.
3rd) An advantage of liquid-fuel engines, such as those of the SLS core stage, is that they can be controlled, have their power adjusted and even be shut down in an emergency, unlike solid engines.
4th) The solid fuel used in the SRBs is composed of a mixture of Liquid Hydrogen and Liquid Oxygen, which must be kept at extremely low (cryogenic) temperatures.
5th) Both the solid and the liquid engines of the SLS work without the need for oxygen, since in space there is no air to sustain combustion.

a) 1st (C) - 2nd (W) - 3rd (C) - 4th (C) - 5th (C)
b) 1st (C) - 2nd (W) - 3rd (C) - 4th (W) - 5th (W)
c) 1st (W) - 2nd (C) - 3rd (W) - 4th (W) - 5th (W)
d) 1st (W) - 2nd (W) - 3rd (C) - 4th (W) - 5th (W)
e) 1st (W) - 2nd (C) - 3rd (W) - 4th (C) - 5th (C)

A missão Artemis II, que levou a tripulação para orbitar a Lua, não tinha um só foguete, mas sim, três foguetes combinados no primeiro estágio. O conjunto recebeu o nome de Sistema de Lançamento Espacial ou em inglês "Space Launch System" (SLS).

O foguete SLS da Missão Artemis II utiliza dois tipos diferentes de propulsão na decolagem. Primeiro: Nas laterais, estão os dois Foguetes de propelente sólido (sigla em inglês SRBs). Estes foguetes são similares aos foguetes de propulsão sólida da OBAFOG, os quais uma vez ligados só desligam quando termina o propelente. Segundo: No centro estão os Motores RS-25 de Combustível Líquido. Estes motores são versáteis, pois são como o acelerador de um carro, ou seja, você pode acelerar "pisando mais forte" no pedal ou desacelerar "aliviando o pé", ou até "tirar o pé".

Atenção: Baseado nas informações contidas no texto e nos seus conhecimentos, PRIMEIRO coloque C, de certo, ou E, de errado, na frente de cada afirmação abaixo e, DEPOIS, assinale a alternativa que contém a sequência correta de C e E.

1ª) Os motores de combustível líquido (RS-25) fornecem a maior parte do empuxo na hora da decolagem, sendo impossíveis de serem desligados após a ignição.
2ª) Os foguetes de combustível sólido (SRBs) são conhecidos por sua alta eficiência e pela facilidade de controlar a potência do empuxo durante o voo, permitindo acelerar ou desacelerar o foguete conforme a necessidade.
3ª) Uma vantagem dos motores de combustível líquido, como os do estágio central do SLS, é que eles podem ser controlados, ter sua potência ajustada e até serem desligados em caso de emergência, ao contrário dos motores sólidos.
4ª) O combustível sólido utilizado nos SRBs é composto por uma mistura de Hidrogênio Líquido e Oxigênio Líquido, que deve ser mantida em temperaturas extremamente baixas (criogênicas).
5ª) Tanto os motores sólidos quanto os líquidos do SLS funcionam sem a necessidade de oxigênio, pois no espaço não existe ar para manter a combustão.

problems.problem:
The engine of the second stage of Artemis II, called the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS), uses a single RL10C-3 engine. It is mainly responsible for the Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI) maneuver, which takes the spacecraft out of Earth orbit and "throws" it towards the Moon. This engine is designed to start and stop several times in vacuum, which is essential to adjust the exact trajectory of the Artemis II mission.

As the engines burn the fuel, the spacecraft becomes lighter, which allows the same amount of force (thrust) to generate a much greater acceleration.

Problem data:
Initial mass of the Upper Stage (with fuel): ~30000 kg
Final mass (after the TLI maneuver, without fuel): ~10000 kg
Thrust of the RL10C-3 engine: 105900 N.

a) Calculate the acceleration of the second stage, with the Orion capsule, with the given initial mass.
b) Calculate the acceleration of the second stage, with the Orion capsule, with the given final mass.
c) Calculate how many times the final acceleration is greater than the initial one, obtained in items a and b.

Mark the alternative that contains the correct answers to items a, b, c, in this order.
a) 3.53 m/s², 11.60 m/s², 3.29
b) 3.53 m/s², 10.59 m/s², 3.00
c) 3.53 m/s², 12.60 m/s², 3.57
d) 10.60 m/s², 3.53 m/s², 0.33
e) 10.60 m/s², 4.53 m/s², 0.43

O motor do segundo estágio da Artemis II, chamado de Estágio de Propulsão Criogênica Provisório (ou Interino) (ICPS) (Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage), utiliza um único motor RL10C-3. Ele é o grande responsável pela manobra de Injeção Trans-Lunar (TLI), que tira a nave da órbita da Terra e a "arremessa" em direção à Lua. Este motor é projetado para ligar e desligar várias vezes no vácuo, o que é essencial para ajustar a trajetória exata da missão Artemis II.

À medida que os motores queimam o combustível, o nave fica mais leve, o que permite que a mesma quantidade de força (empuxo) gere uma aceleração muito maior.

Dados do Problema:
Massa Inicial do Estágio Superior (com combustível): ~30.000 kg
Massa Final (após a manobra TLI, sem combustível): ~10.000 kg
Empuxo do Motor RL10C-3: 105.900 N.

a) Calcule a aceleração do segundo estágio, com a cápsula Órion, com a massa inicial dada.
b) Calcule a aceleração do segundo estágio, com a cápsula Órion, com a massa final dada.
c) Calcule quantas vezes a aceleração final é maior do que a inicial, obtidas nos itens a e b.

Assinale a alternativa que contém as respostas corretas aos itens a, b, c, nesta ordem.
a) 3,53 m/s², 11,60 m/s², 3,29
b) 3,53 m/s², 10,59 m/s², 3,00
c) 3,53 m/s², 12,60 m/s², 3,57
d) 10,60 m/s², 3,53 m/s², 0,33
e) 10,60 m/s², 4,53 m/s², 0,43

problems.problem:
The motion of the PET-bottle rocket, launched obliquely, is the composition of Uniform Rectilinear Motion (URM) in the horizontal and of Uniformly Varied Rectilinear Motion (UVRM) in the vertical, and the basic equations of URM and UVRM are given by the four equations below (assuming the $y$ axis pointing upwards), which are sufficient to solve any ballistic motion problem without air resistance.

$$V_x(t)=V_{0x}\ \ (\text{Eq. 1})\qquad\text{and}\qquad x(t)=V_{0x}\,t\ \ (\text{Eq. 2})$$

$$V_y(t)=V_{0y}-gt\ \ (\text{Eq. 3})\qquad\text{and}\qquad y(t)=V_{0y}\,t-\frac{1}{2}gt^2\ \ (\text{Eq. 4})$$

Remembering that: $V_{0x}=V_0\cos\theta_0$ (Eq. 5) and $V_{0y}=V_0\sin\theta_0$ (Eq. 6)

where $V_0$ is the speed with which the rocket is launched, $\theta_0$ is the angle relative to the ground at which the rocket was launched, assumed here to be 45 degrees, and the local gravitational acceleration is $g = 10.0\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. $V_x$ and $V_y$ are the horizontal and vertical components of the velocity at any instant $t$. $V_{0x}$ and $V_{0y}$ are the horizontal and vertical velocities at the initial instant of the launch, respectively.

At the highest point of the motion of the rocket, when launched at any angle relative to the ground (except an angle equal to zero), the vertical component of the velocity vector is zero. That is, at the top of the parabola the vertical component of the velocity vector is zero, that is, $V_y = 0$.

Consider that a PET-bottle rocket was launched with initial speed $V_0 = 80\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Mark the alternative that contains the correct values of the maximum range, $X_{max}$, and maximum height, $Y_{max}$, reached by the rocket, in this order. Given: $\cos 45^\circ = \sin 45^\circ = 0.7$. Use $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Suggestion: calculate the rise time to $Y_{max}$.
a) 637.2 m and 157.8 m.
b) 627.8 m and 156.0 m.
c) 627.2 m and 156.8 m.
d) 607.8 m and 146.8 m.
e) 650.0 m and 1550.0 m.

O movimento do foguete de garrafa PET, lançado de forma oblíqua é a composição do Movimento Retilíneo e Uniforme (MRU) na horizontal e do Movimento Retilíneo Uniformemente Variado (MRUV) na vertical e as equações básicas do MRU e do MRUV são dadas pelas quatro equações abaixo (supondo o eixo $y$ apontando para cima), as quais são suficientes para resolver qualquer problema de movimento balístico sem a resistência do ar.

$$V_x(t)=V_{0x}\ \ (\text{Eq. 1})\qquad\text{e}\qquad x(t)=V_{0x}\,t\ \ (\text{Eq. 2})$$

$$V_y(t)=V_{0y}-gt\ \ (\text{Eq. 3})\qquad\text{e}\qquad y(t)=V_{0y}\,t-\frac{1}{2}gt^2\ \ (\text{Eq. 4})$$

Lembrando que: $V_{0x}=V_0\cos\theta_0$ (Eq. 5) e $V_{0y}=V_0\sin\theta_0$ (Eq. 6)

Onde $V_0$ é a velocidade com que o foguete é lançado, $\theta_0$ é o ângulo em relação ao solo no qual o foguete foi lançado, estamos supondo a 45 graus, a aceleração gravitacional local é $g = 10{,}0\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. $V_x$ e $V_y$ são as componentes das velocidades horizontal e vertical respectivamente num instante $t$ qualquer. $V_{0x}$ e $V_{0y}$ são as velocidades horizontal e vertical no instante inicial do lançamento, respectivamente.

No ponto mais alto do movimento do foguete, quando lançado em qualquer ângulo em relação ao solo (exceto no ângulo igual a zero) a componente do vetor velocidade na vertical é zero. Ou seja, no topo da parábola a componente do vetor velocidade na vertical é zero, isto é, $V_y = 0$.

Considere que um foguete de garrafa PET foi lançado com velocidade inicial $V_0 = 80\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Assinale a alternativa que contém os valores corretos do alcance máximo, $X_{max}$, e altura máxima, $Y_{max}$, atingida pelo foguete, nesta ordem. Dado: $\cos 45^\circ = \sin 45^\circ = 0{,}7$. Use $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Sugestão: Calcule o tempo de subida até o $Y_{max}$.
a) 637,2 m e 157,8 m.
b) 627,8 m e 156,0 m.
c) 627,2 m e 156,8 m.
d) 607,8 m e 146,8 m.
e) 650,0 m e 1550,0 m.
